title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
克己復禮爲仁
劉啓東
同考試官訓導王　批〔論語題似易而實難非的有見者辭多悖理况克復處尤難體貼此作辭不煩而意〕
自足本房之冠舍子其誰
考試官學正秦　批〔理學文字簡明似此者蓋不〕
===
考試官教授徐　批〔講克復處良是〕
去其不可有而還其所固有則心之德全矣蓋
私欲於身不可有而禮則吾之所固有者也人
能克而復之則心德豈有不全者哉夫子因顔
淵問仁而告之以此蓋謂己者吾身之私欲己
有不克則有以害吾之仁矣禮者天理之節文
禮有不復則無以全吾之仁矣故一念方形欲
心或有所萌動則力以勝之如將之克敵于以
復吾之規矩而有所持循七情已發欲心或有
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

克己復禮爲仁。

劉啓東

同考試官訓導王批〔論語題似易而實難，非的有見者，辭多悖理。况克復處尤難體貼，此作辭不煩而意〕自足，本房之冠，舍子其誰？

考試官學正秦批〔理學文字，簡明似此者，蓋不〕

考試官教授徐批〔講克復處良是。〕

去其不可有，而還其所固有，則心之德全矣。蓋私欲於身不可有，而禮則吾之所固有者也。人能克而復之，則心德豈有不全者哉？夫子因顔淵問仁，而告之以此。蓋謂己者，吾身之私欲；己有不克，則有以害吾之仁矣。禮者，天理之節文；禮有不復，則無以全吾之仁矣。故一念方形，欲心或有所萌動，則力以勝之，如將之克敵，于以復吾之規矩，而有所持循；七情已發，欲心或有
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“To overcome the self and return to ritual propriety constitutes humaneness.”

Liu Qidong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: “Topics from the Analects seem easy but are actually difficult. Unless a writer possesses genuine insight, his words often run counter to principle. Moreover, overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety are especially difficult to grasp intimately. This composition is concise in wording yet complete in meaning. Who but you could rank first in this examining room?”

Comment by Examiner Qin, Instructor: “Among writings on the learning of principle, those as concise and clear as this are surely not …” [?]

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The explanation of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety is very sound.”

Remove what one must not possess and restore what one inherently possesses, and the virtue of the mind will be complete. Selfish desires are what one must not harbor within oneself, while ritual propriety is what one inherently possesses. If a person can overcome those desires and return to propriety, how could the virtue of the mind fail to be complete? When Yan Yuan asked about humaneness, the Master instructed him in these terms. His meaning was that the self consists of the selfish desires within us. If any aspect of the self remains unconquered, it can injure our humaneness. Ritual propriety is the articulated pattern of heavenly principle. If any aspect of propriety remains unrestored, we have no means of bringing our humaneness to completion. Thus, when a thought is just taking shape and the desiring mind begins to stir, we must exert ourselves to overcome it, as a commander defeats an enemy. In this way we recover our standards and have something to uphold and follow. When the seven emotions have arisen, the desiring mind may …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
所縱放則决以去之如水之制火于以歸吾之
發率而有所執守肌膚之會以固邪僞無由而
內入動容周旋自中乎禮也筋骸之束以堅非
僻奚從而外至動靜云爲自合乎中也克去已
私復歸於禮由是向焉天理人欲每相雜於吾
前今則人欲泯天者定太空無雲而靈臺爲之
湛然本心之德復全於我矣昔焉人心道心每
相攻於吾內今則危者安微者著明鏡不塵而
爲之泰回有之善復甫於我矣吁加克
===
功全本心德爲仁之道外此其何以哉
嗟乎問仁多矣唯顏淵告之以此盖夫子授以
傳道之心法也理在天下曰道道切人身曰仁
斯道也曾子得之曰誠正子思得之曰戒懼孟
子得之曰明誠伊洛諸儒千言萬語皆不外此
也聖賢之言具在方冊欲爲仁者請事斯語
博厚所以載物也高明所以覆物也
趙繼英
此題場中作者類能言之
同考試官訓導汪　批
punctuated:
所縱放，則决以去之，如水之制火，于以歸吾之發率，而有所執守。肌膚之會以固，邪僞無由而內入，動容周旋自中乎禮也；筋骸之束以堅，非僻奚從而外至，動靜云爲自合乎中也。克去已私，復歸於禮。由是向焉，天理人欲每相雜於吾前，今則人欲泯、天者定，太空無雲，而靈臺爲之湛然，本心之德復全於我矣。昔焉，人心道心每相攻於吾內，今則危者安、微者著，明鏡不塵，而爲之泰，回有之善復甫於我矣。吁！加克功，全本心德，爲仁之道，外此其何以哉？
嗟乎！問仁多矣，唯顏淵告之以此，盖夫子授以傳道之心法也。理在天下曰道，道切人身曰仁。斯道也，曾子得之曰誠正，子思得之曰戒懼，孟子得之曰明誠，伊洛諸儒千言萬語皆不外此也。聖賢之言具在方冊，欲爲仁者，請事斯語。
博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也。
趙繼英
此題場中作者類能言之。
同考試官訓導汪，批。
translation_en:
…are allowed free rein, then resolutely remove them, as water subdues fire, thereby returning to the proper course of one's expression [?] and having something to hold fast to. When the body's integument is secured, depravity and falsity have no way to enter within, and one's bearing and movements naturally accord with ritual propriety. When the binding of sinews and bones is firm, how can perversity approach from without? In movement and stillness, speech and action, one naturally accords with the mean. Overcome and eliminate selfish desires, and return to ritual propriety. Formerly, heavenly principle and human desires were constantly intermingled before me; now human desires disappear and what belongs to Heaven is settled. Like a cloudless sky, the mind becomes limpid, and the virtue of my original mind is once again complete within me. In the past, the human mind and the mind of the Way constantly contended within me; now what was precarious becomes secure, and what was subtle becomes manifest. The bright mirror gathers no dust, and there is tranquility; inherent goodness is restored within me [?]. Ah! Apply the effort of self-mastery and make whole the virtue of the original mind: what other means could there be for practicing benevolence?
Alas! Many asked about benevolence, but only Yan Yuan was instructed in these terms. This was surely the Master's transmission to him of the method of the mind by which the Way is handed down. Principle as it exists throughout the world is called the Way; the Way as it bears directly upon one's person is called benevolence. This Way, as apprehended by Zengzi, was called sincerity and rectification; as apprehended by Zisi, vigilance and apprehension; as apprehended by Mengzi, understanding and sincerity. The countless words of the Confucian scholars of the Yi and Luo tradition never went beyond this. The words of the sages and worthies are fully preserved in books. Those who wish to practice benevolence should put these words into practice.
“Breadth and depth are the means by which things are borne; height and brightness are the means by which things are sheltered.”
Zhao Jiying
“Those writing on this topic in the examination hall were generally able to discuss it.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor.

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
俱於博厚高明處講究精切此卷分析曉然必嘗究心理學者
同考試官訓導逯　批〔寫出聖人與天地同用之意不泛不畧宜冠本房〕
置高選
同考試官訓導朱　批〔講覆載處迥異衆作宜〕
考試官學正秦　批〔明淨可錄〕
考試官教授李　批〔詞整而理足〕
中庸論聖德之者所積同乎地之用所發同乎
天盍聖人之德一誠而已則其所積所發
===
與天地　其用哉中庸發明天道之意如
此謂夫聖人至誠之德存於中者不息而有常
驗於外也悠遠而無窮自其悠遠所積者言之
仁恩覃被浩乎廣博初無涯涘之可窺德澤弘
施淵乎深厚初無限量之可測持載之妙有形
有色悉奠於化育之區負荷之神無小無大咸
安於長養之域彼至哉坤元萬物載焉地之用
廣矣聖人之博厚載物如此與地何殊哉自其
博厚所發者言之功業之成巍然高大而卓冠
punctuated:
俱於博厚高明處講究精切，此卷分析曉然，必嘗究心理學者。
同考試官訓導逯批〔寫出聖人與天地同用之意，不泛不畧，宜冠本房〕。置高選。
同考試官訓導朱批〔講覆載處迥異衆作，宜〕。
考試官學正秦批〔明淨可錄〕。
考試官教授李批〔詞整而理足〕。
中庸論聖德之者，所積同乎地之用，所發同乎天。盍聖人之德一誠而已，則其所積所發，與天地其用哉？中庸發明天道之意如此。謂夫聖人至誠之德，存於中者不息而有常，驗於外也悠遠而無窮。自其悠遠所積者言之，仁恩覃被，浩乎廣博，初無涯涘之可窺；德澤弘施，淵乎深厚，初無限量之可測。持載之妙，有形有色，悉奠於化育之區；負荷之神，無小無大，咸安於長養之域。彼至哉坤元，萬物載焉，地之用廣矣。聖人之博厚載物如此，與地何殊哉？自其博厚所發者言之，功業之成，巍然高大而卓冠
translation_en:
All discuss breadth and depth, height and brightness with precision and penetration. This essay analyzes them with unmistakable clarity; its author must have devoted himself to the study of principle.
Associate Examiner Lu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔It brings out the idea that the sage shares the workings of Heaven and Earth, without being vague or cursory. It should rank first in this examining room.〕 Place it among the highest selections.
Associate Examiner Zhu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Its discussion of sheltering and bearing things is markedly different from the other essays. It should…〕 [The recommendation appears displaced in the transcription; “Place it among the highest selections” occurs above.]
Examiner Qin, an Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and cleanly written; worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Li, a Professor, comments: 〔The phrasing is orderly and the reasoning fully developed.〕
The Doctrine of the Mean discusses sagely virtue [?]: what it accumulates accords with the workings of Earth, and what it manifests accords with Heaven. Since the sage’s virtue is simply sincerity, how could what it accumulates and manifests fail to share the workings of Heaven and Earth [?]? Such is the Doctrine of the Mean’s explanation of the Way of Heaven. It means that the sage’s virtue of utmost sincerity, abiding within, is unceasing and constant; as evidenced outwardly, it endures far into the distance without limit.
Speaking of what is accumulated through this enduring reach: benevolent kindness extends everywhere, vast in its breadth, with no shore or boundary that one can discern; virtuous beneficence spreads widely, profound in its depth, with no limit that one can measure. Through the marvel of its sustaining power, everything possessing form and appearance is settled within the sphere of transformation and nurture. Through the wondrous efficacy of its bearing power, everything, small or great, rests secure within the domain of growth and nourishment. “Perfect indeed is the primal power of Kun”: all things are borne upon it, and broad indeed are the workings of Earth. The sage’s breadth and depth bear all things in this way; how do they differ from Earth?
Speaking of what manifests from this breadth and depth: the achievements of his endeavors stand lofty and great, preeminently surpassing…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
羣倫文章之盛煥乎昭明而光被四表凡林林
而生者皆在所包含曲成之而不遺也總總而
聚者皆在所照臨徧覆之而無外也彼大哉乾
元萬物覆焉天之用大矣聖人之高明覆物如
此與天何異哉吁天地至大也而至誠之功用
同之此聖人所以參天地而爲三也歟抑又論
之此特言聖人與天地同用耳下文又曰博厚
配地高明配天悠久無疆則言聖人與天地同
然天能覆而不能載地能載而不能覆聖
===
人輔相
乎天地而天地且有賴於聖人矣此又不可不
知
智之實知斯二者弗去是也
韓宗福
同考試官教諭倪　批　〔講弗去處親切有味必充蹈者吾於子不獨取其文也〕
同考試官教諭李　批　〔發揮智之實殆盡〕
考試官學正秦　批　〔明淨無疵〕
punctuated:
羣倫，文章之盛，煥乎昭明而光被四表。凡林林而生者，皆在所包含，曲成之而不遺也；總總而聚者，皆在所照臨，徧覆之而無外也。彼大哉乾元，萬物覆焉，天之用大矣！聖人之高明覆物如此，與天何異哉？吁！天地至大也，而至誠之功用同之，此聖人所以參天地而爲三也歟？抑又論之，此特言聖人與天地同用耳。下文又曰：「博厚配地，高明配天，悠久無疆。」則言聖人與天地同。然天能覆而不能載，地能載而不能覆，聖人輔相乎天地，而天地且有賴於聖人矣。此又不可不知。

智之實，知斯二者弗去是也。
韓宗福

同考試官教諭倪，批：〔講弗去處親切有味，必充蹈者，吾於子不獨取其文也。〕
同考試官教諭李，批：〔發揮智之實殆盡。〕
考試官學正秦，批：〔明淨無疵。〕
translation_en:
…above all others. The splendor of his cultural accomplishments shines brilliantly, its light reaching the four outer bounds. All the teeming things that live are embraced within his compass: he brings each to fulfillment according to its particular nature, leaving none behind. All the multitudes that gather lie within his illumination: he shelters them everywhere, excluding none. How great is the primal power of Qian! All things are sheltered beneath it; vast indeed is Heaven’s operation! The sage’s loftiness and brilliance shelter things in this way: how does this differ from Heaven? Ah! Heaven and Earth are supremely great, yet the efficacy of utmost sincerity equals theirs. Is this not why the sage stands alongside Heaven and Earth to form a triad? To discuss this further, this passage speaks only of the sage sharing the operation of Heaven and Earth. The text below further says: “His breadth and depth match Earth; his loftiness and brilliance match Heaven; his endurance has no bounds.” This speaks of the sage being the same as Heaven and Earth. Yet Heaven can shelter but cannot support, and Earth can support but cannot shelter. The sage assists Heaven and Earth, and even Heaven and Earth depend upon him. This, too, must be understood.

“The substance of wisdom consists in knowing these two things and not departing from them.”
By Han Zongfu.

Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of ‘not departing’ is direct and full of meaning. He must be one who fully puts it into practice [?]. In you, I value more than your writing alone.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “He expounds the substance of wisdom almost exhaustively.”

Examiner Qin, School Director, comments: “Clear, clean, and without blemish.”

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授李　批　〔簡當宜錄〕
大賢論智之所以爲智在知道之明而守之固
也蓋道莫大於孝弟也於斯二者知之明而守
之固非智之實而何哉昔孟子論仁義之實至
此謂夫明義理識時勢智固無所不知矣而其
爲道不有切近精實者乎知古今達事變智固
無所不通矣而其爲道不有近裏著己者乎蓋
孝以事親固爲仁之實矣智則識見內融眞知
□□之經地之義也而非外鑠之物弟以
===
□爲義□實矣智則神明內緼灼見其爲
民之彝也物之則也而非遠人之道知不徒知
必祇服文事而始終之無間一出言而不敢忘
一□□足而不敢忘也見不徒見必克念天顯而
久暫之如一造次必於是顚沛必於是也夫如
是則其知也非聞見之知所謂無所不知者皆
發端於此矣其見也非皮膚之見所謂無所不
通者皆托始於此矣然則智之所以爲智者豈
可舍是而他求哉吁仁義之實固在於孝弟而
punctuated:
考試官教授李批〔簡當宜錄〕

大賢論智之所以爲智，在知道之明而守之固也。蓋道莫大於孝弟也，於斯二者知之明而守之固，非智之實而何哉？昔孟子論仁義之實，至此謂夫明義理、識時勢，智固無所不知矣，而其爲道不有切近精實者乎？知古今、達事變，智固無所不通矣，而其爲道不有近裏著己者乎？蓋孝以事親，固爲仁之實矣。智則識見內融，眞知□□之經、地之義也，而非外鑠之物。弟以□爲義□實矣，智則神明內緼，灼見其爲民之彝也、物之則也，而非遠人之道。知不徒知，必祇服文事而始終之無間，一出言而不敢忘，一□□足而不敢忘也。見不徒見，必克念天顯而久暫之如一，造次必於是，顚沛必於是也。夫如是，則其知也非聞見之知，所謂無所不知者皆發端於此矣；其見也非皮膚之見，所謂無所不通者皆托始於此矣。然則智之所以爲智者，豈可舍是而他求哉？吁！仁義之實固在於孝弟，而
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: 〔Concise and apt; it merits inclusion.〕

The great worthy explained that what makes wisdom wisdom lies in understanding the Way clearly and holding firmly to it. For nothing in the Way is greater than filial devotion and fraternal respect. To understand these two clearly and hold firmly to them—what could this be but the substance of wisdom? When Mencius discussed the substance of benevolence and righteousness, he came to this point: in discerning moral principles and recognizing the circumstances of the times, wisdom certainly leaves nothing unknown. Yet does its practice not have something close at hand, essential, and substantial? In knowing past and present and comprehending changing affairs, wisdom certainly leaves nothing uncomprehended. Yet does its practice not have something inward and directly pertinent to oneself?

Filial devotion, through which one serves one’s parents, is indeed the substance of benevolence. Wisdom inwardly integrates understanding and insight, truly knowing that this is the constant norm of [illegible] and the rightness of Earth [?], rather than something imposed from outside. Fraternal respect, through [illegible], constitutes the substance of righteousness [?]. Wisdom stores spiritual illumination within, clearly perceiving that this is the enduring norm of the people and the governing rule of things, rather than a Way remote from human beings. Knowing must not remain mere knowing: one must reverently attend to civil duties [?], without interruption from beginning to end, never daring to forget in uttering a word or in any … movement of the feet [?]. Seeing must not remain mere seeing: one must keep Heaven’s manifest principles in mind, remaining constant over long and short periods alike. Even in haste one must abide by these; even in adversity one must abide by these.

If this is so, such knowledge is no mere knowledge acquired through hearing and seeing: what is called leaving nothing unknown all begins here. Such insight is no superficial insight: what is called leaving nothing uncomprehended all takes its origin here. How, then, could one abandon this and seek elsewhere what makes wisdom wisdom? Ah! The substance of benevolence and righteousness assuredly lies in filial devotion and fraternal respect, and …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
智之實亦不外乎孝弟孟子以是爲言其開示
人心之意深且切矣大抵事親從兄乃良心之
發而人心之所同也天下之道皆原於此然必
知之明而守之固然後節之密而樂之深也柰
何戰國之時人心陷溺墨子以兼愛爲仁楊子
以爲我爲義至於縱橫遊說之徒徧滿天下不
知斯道爲何物孟子目擊其弊而此章反覆詳
明以曉告之可謂緊爲人處也惜乎當世之人
□□莫□啓也意
===
忠信所以進德也修辭立其誠所以居業
也
韓宗福
同考試官教諭倪　批〔此題場中作者不腐則泛殊爲可厭是篇能融會本義成文平淡醇雅殆絲竹繁奏而希聲窈渺者歟〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔此□內外交修之功場中作者多平平說去殊無意義惟此作曉然且說理真切是必不怠於進修者也〕
考試官學正秦　批〔說理明白必嘗用心於內者〕
punctuated:
智之實亦不外乎孝弟。孟子以是爲言，其開示人心之意深且切矣。大抵事親從兄，乃良心之發，而人心之所同也。天下之道皆原於此，然必知之明而守之固，然後節之密而樂之深也。柰何戰國之時，人心陷溺，墨子以兼愛爲仁，楊子以爲我爲義，至於縱橫遊說之徒，徧滿天下，不知斯道爲何物。孟子目擊其弊，而此章反覆詳明以曉告之，可謂緊爲人處也。惜乎當世之人，□□莫□啓也。意

忠信所以進德也，修辭立其誠所以居業也。

韓宗福

同考試官教諭倪　批〔此題場中作者不腐則泛殊爲可厭是篇能融會本義成文平淡醇雅殆絲竹繁奏而希聲窈渺者歟〕

同考試官教諭李　批〔此□內外交修之功場中作者多平平說去殊無意義惟此作曉然且說理真切是必不怠於進修者也〕

考試官學正秦　批〔說理明白必嘗用心於內者〕
translation_en:
…the substance of wisdom likewise lies nowhere beyond filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. In speaking thus, Mengzi’s intention to enlighten people’s hearts was profound and urgent. Serving one’s parents and following one’s elder brothers are, in general, expressions of the innate moral heart, shared by all human hearts. All the principles of the world originate here. Yet one must understand them clearly and hold to them firmly before one can regulate them precisely and delight in them deeply. Alas, in the Warring States period, people’s hearts became engulfed in error. Mozi took universal love for benevolence, and Yangzi took acting for oneself for righteousness. As for the itinerant persuaders advocating rival alliances, they filled the world without knowing what this Way was. Mengzi witnessed these failings, and in this chapter explained the matter repeatedly and fully to enlighten people. This may indeed be called a passage urgently concerned with helping others. Regrettably, the people of that age … could not … be enlightened [?]. “Intention” [?].

“Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue; refining one’s words and establishing sincerity are the means of abiding in one’s undertaking.”

Han Zongfu

Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor, comments: 〔Among those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic, their work was either stale or vague—particularly tiresome. This essay integrates the fundamental meaning into a composition that is plain, pure, and elegant. Might it be that rare, faint, far-reaching note amid a profusion of strings and pipes?〕

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔This [illegible character] concerns the work of cultivating both the inner and the outer aspects of oneself. Most candidates in the examination hall treated it in a pedestrian fashion, with scarcely any meaningful substance. This composition alone is lucid, and its exposition of principle is true and pertinent. Its author must surely be someone who does not slacken in moral advancement and cultivation.〕

Examiner Qin, Instructor, comments: 〔His exposition of principle is clear. He must have devoted effort to his inner cultivation.〕

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授李　批〔簡明說理文字當選〕
文言論乾九三君子學之誠乎內者有學之
誠乎外者蓋學不外乎一誠也內外交致其功
德業之所以盛者有由然哉昔文言申九三乾
惕之意若謂君子身處乎危厲之地故心
之進修之誠彼理之得於心者德也心有不
誠則念皆妄矣德何自而進耶必主於心者真
實無妄而邪心之不形所謂毋載爾偽者是已
省至不欺而偽妄之不雜所謂毋貳
===
毫私意自蔽日新又新駸駸乎自造於廣大之
矣天理常在不以一毫私欲自累日就月將
乎自造於高明之境矣忠信所以進德君
乾惕若者非以此歟夫既有忠信以誠於
內又可不修辭以誠於外乎彼理之見於事者
業也辭之不修則誠不立矣業何自而居耶必
發於言者躁妄是禁而言為有物使吾心之誠
確乎不拔也出於口者鄙悖斯遠而言為可法
punctuated:
考試官教授李，批〔簡明說理，文字當選。〕

文言論乾九三，君子學之誠乎內者，有學之誠乎外者。蓋學不外乎一誠也，內外交致其功，德業之所以盛者有由然哉！昔文言申九三乾惕之意，若謂君子身處乎危厲之地，故心之進修之誠。彼理之得於心者，德也。心有不誠，則念皆妄矣，德何自而進耶？必主於心者真實無妄，而邪心之不形，所謂「毋載爾偽」者是已。省至不欺，而偽妄之不雜，所謂「毋貳」。毫私意自蔽，日新又新，駸駸乎自造於廣大之矣。天理常在，不以一毫私欲自累，日就月將，乎自造於高明之境矣。忠信所以進德，君乾惕若者，非以此歟？夫既有忠信以誠於內，又可不修辭以誠於外乎？彼理之見於事者，業也。辭之不修，則誠不立矣，業何自而居耶？必發於言者躁妄是禁，而言為有物，使吾心之誠確乎不拔也。出於口者鄙悖斯遠，而言為可法。
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔The reasoning is explained simply and clearly; this composition deserves selection.〕

In discussing the third yang line of Qian, the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) speaks of the gentleman’s learning as making him sincere within and of learning as making him sincere without. For learning does not extend beyond sincerity alone. When effort is applied both inwardly and outwardly, surely there is a reason why virtue and undertakings flourish! Formerly, when the Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborated upon the diligence and vigilance of the third yang line, it seemed to say that the gentleman occupies a perilous position, and therefore his mind is sincere in advancing and cultivating himself [?]. Principle apprehended in the mind is virtue. If the mind lacks sincerity, its thoughts are all false: how, then, can virtue advance? What governs the mind must be genuine and free of falsity, so that deviant intentions do not arise. This is what is meant by “Do not practice your deceit.” Through self-examination, one reaches the point of being without deception, with no admixture of falsity: this is what is meant by “Do not be double-minded.” The passage concerning obscuring oneself with the slightest selfish intention is defective [?]. Renewing oneself daily, and renewing oneself yet again, one steadily advances of oneself toward breadth and greatness [?]. Heavenly principle is constantly present; without allowing the slightest selfish desire to encumber oneself, one progresses day by day and month by month, advancing of oneself into the realm of loftiness and illumination [?]. Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue. Is this not what underlies the gentleman’s diligence and vigilance [?]?

Now, once one has loyalty and trustworthiness to become sincere within, can one also fail to refine one’s words in order to become sincere without? Principle manifested in affairs constitutes one’s undertakings. If words are not refined, sincerity is not established: how, then, can one abide in one’s undertakings? In what one expresses in speech, rashness and falsity must be restrained, and one’s words must have substance, so that the sincerity of one’s mind is firmly established and cannot be uprooted. In what issues from one’s mouth, vulgarity and perversity must be kept far away, and one’s words must be fit to serve as a model …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
使在心之實堅乎不渝也夫誠修於外則措諸
躬者無非可常之事充積之盛馴致乎可大矣
見之外者無非可蹈之實光輝之著漸極於富
有矣修辭立誠所以居業君子乾乾惕若者非
歟吁合內外於一心之誠致進修於德業
君子取德之學斯其至矣抑論之忠信心
蘊於心者所以見於事修業事也實於言者
所以養其心一人之學內外一誠交相警發又
息之哉若湯之日新又新文王之純
===
於德業之間噫微斯人吾誰與歸
周公憂勤惕厲皆所以極此心之誠
備致用立成器以為天下利莫大乎聖
人
劉乾亨
同考試官教諭倪　批〔揭書命題本自平易作者往往鑿意求之多以下 盤入艱深本旨此篇理足而氣充令人愈讀而愈有味蓋嘗潛心易學而有得者乎〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔此題體認不真則與意思重〕
punctuated:
使在心之實堅乎不渝也。夫誠修於外，則措諸躬者無非可常之事，充積之盛，馴致乎可大矣；見之外者無非可蹈之實，光輝之著，漸極於富有矣。修辭立誠，所以居業。君子乾乾惕若者，非歟？吁！合內外於一心之誠，致進修於德業，君子取德之學，斯其至矣！抑論之，忠信，心蘊於心者，所以見於事；修業，事也，實於言者，所以養其心。一人之學，內外一誠，交相警發，又息之哉？若湯之日新又新，文王之純於德業之間。噫！微斯人，吾誰與歸？周公憂勤惕厲，皆所以極此心之誠。

備致用，立成器以為天下利，莫大乎聖人。

劉乾亨

同考試官教諭倪　批〔揭書命題，本自平易，作者往往鑿意求之，多以下 盤入艱深本旨。此篇理足而氣充，令人愈讀而愈有味，蓋嘗潛心易學而有得者乎〕

同考試官教諭李　批〔此題體認不真，則與意思重〕
translation_en:
…making the genuineness within the heart firm and unchanging. When sincerity is cultivated outwardly, everything put into personal practice is something that can be sustained. Its abundant accumulation gradually attains greatness. Everything manifested outwardly is a concrete reality that can be acted upon; its manifest brilliance gradually reaches plenitude. Refining one’s words and establishing sincerity are the means of securing one’s undertakings. Is this not why the gentleman labors unceasingly and remains vigilant [?]? Ah! Uniting inner and outer in the sincerity of a single heart, and bringing advancement and cultivation to virtue and undertakings: here the gentleman’s learning in acquiring virtue reaches its utmost!

To discuss this further: loyalty and trustworthiness—the heart’s store within the heart [?]—are what find expression in affairs. Cultivating one’s undertakings concerns affairs; making one’s words genuine is what nourishes the heart. In a person’s learning, inward and outward share a single sincerity, each alerting and stimulating the other. How could this ever cease? Such were Tang’s renewal day after day and King Wen’s purity amid virtue and undertakings [?]. Alas! Without such men, with whom could I associate? The Duke of Zhou’s anxious diligence and vigilant exertion all served to bring the sincerity of this heart to its utmost.

“In providing for use [?] and establishing finished implements for the benefit of all under Heaven, none is greater than the sage.”

Liu Qianheng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor: 〔A topic drawn from a book is inherently straightforward. Writers often force interpretations in seeking its meaning, frequently plunging into abstruseness [the wording concerning the original purport is garbled: ?]. This essay is ample in reasoning and full of vigor; the more one reads it, the more rewarding it becomes. Perhaps its author has devoted himself to studying the Book of Changes and gained insight from it?〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔If this topic is not truly apprehended, then its ideas will overlap [?]…〕

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
畳難於措詞是篇條暢而有則宜錄以式學者
考試官學正秦　批　易學文字潔淨似此篇者絶少
考試官教授李　批　前作之人歸功於聖人深得本旨
盡制作之人在制作之人蓋制作以利民爲大
夫用無不周而人無不利者非聖人其孰
哉昔之傳論造化人事功用之大以明著
功用大謂夫上古之時人皆莫知其用聖
人則制器以□民用彼萬物散殊有可爲揀宇
□可爲組者焉必備此物以致居處被
===
□則宮衣裳之制以定有章有服而成
器不於此而□乎百物不廢有可爲服乘者焉
□可紀事者焉必具是物以致引重明決之
□書契之制以成同軌同文而成器又
此而立乎由是使天下之人宮室以安其
居衣服以華其身措世道於一新之會利其利
而莫知誰之所爲也車輿以通民財書契以察
□偽妙黎元於於變之機宜其宜而莫知誰之
所使也然此果何人能之哉惟在於有德位之
punctuated:
畳，難於措詞。是篇條暢而有則，宜錄以式學者。
考試官學正秦　批：易學文字潔淨似此篇者絶少。
考試官教授李　批：前作之人歸功於聖人，深得本旨。
盡制作之人在制作之人，蓋制作以利民爲大。夫用無不周而人無不利者，非聖人其孰哉？昔之傳論造化人事功用之大，以明著功用大，謂夫上古之時，人皆莫知其用，聖人則制器以□民用。彼萬物散殊，有可爲揀宇□可爲組者焉，必備此物以致居處被□，則宮衣裳之制以定，有章有服，而成器不於此而□乎？百物不廢，有可爲服乘者焉，□可紀事者焉，必具是物以致引重明決之□，書契之制以成，同軌同文，而成器又此而立乎？由是使天下之人，宮室以安其居，衣服以華其身，措世道於一新之會，利其利而莫知誰之所爲也；車輿以通民財，書契以察□偽，妙黎元於於變之機，宜其宜而莫知誰之所使也。然此果何人能之哉？惟在於有德位之
translation_en:
…overlap, making the wording difficult. This essay is lucid, fluent, and well ordered; it deserves to be recorded as a model for students.
Examiner Qin, an Instructor, comments: Writings on the Changes as clean and precise as this essay are exceedingly rare.
Examiner Li, a Professor, comments: The person who composed the preceding work attributes the achievement to the sages, grasping the fundamental meaning profoundly.
Those who fully accomplish making and instituting lie in those who make and institute [?], for the greatest purpose of making and instituting is to benefit the people. Who but a sage could provide for every use and benefit everyone? The Commentary of old discusses the great efficacy of the transformations of nature and of human affairs, thereby making manifest the greatness of their efficacy [?]. This means that in highest antiquity people did not know how to put things to use, but the sages fashioned implements to □ the people's uses [?]. The myriad things are diverse and dispersed: some can serve for buildings [?], and □ can serve for woven bands. These materials must be assembled to provide dwellings and clothing [?]. Thus the forms of buildings and garments were established, with patterns and attire; were finished implements not thereby □ [?]? None of the hundred kinds of things was left unused. Some could serve for conveyance, and □ could record affairs. These materials must be provided to enable the hauling of heavy loads and clear determinations [?]. The system of written tallies was completed, with uniform carriage tracks and uniform writing; were finished implements thereby established as well [?]?
Through this, people throughout the realm had palaces and houses to make their dwellings secure, and clothing to adorn their persons. The course of the age was brought to a moment of complete renewal: people enjoyed its benefits without knowing who had brought them about. Carts and carriages circulated the people's goods, and written tallies enabled the scrutiny of □ and fraud [?]. The common people were wondrously brought to the point of transformation [?]: they enjoyed what suited their needs without knowing who had made it so. Yet who could actually accomplish this? It rests solely with one possessing virtue and position …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人而已哉以智者固善於創物矣然能一而
不能二非所以爲大也惟聖人出類拔萃智足
以周物于物之至粗者而知有至精者寓故能
盡此變通之妙而利及乎天下智者能彷彿其
𨚫巧者固善於述之矣然宜此而不能宜
此宜民之神〔所〕以爲大也惟聖人首出庶物明足以
理〔之〕之至微者而知有至妙者存故能盡
此宜民之神〔所〕爲法於天下巧者能窺測其一
制作於聖人而垂範妙於無窮此聖
===
以爲大著龜功用之大於斯亦可見矣
抑論制器尚象不世之大功制度考文三王之
重政變通之妙以爲天下利者非聖人之
也所於易之象而後成耳亦非一人能之
數世數聖人而後備焉斯人生生之道若
此其難而聖人所以生生斯人若此其勞也故
曰如古時無聖人人之類滅久矣信夫
書
八音克諧無相奪倫
punctuated:
聖人而已哉！以智者固善於創物矣，然能一而不能二，非所以爲大也。惟聖人出類拔萃，智足以周物，于物之至粗者而知有至精者寓，故能盡此變通之妙，而利及乎天下。智者能彷彿其𨚫，巧者固善於述之矣，然宜此而不能宜此，宜民之神〔所〕以爲大也。惟聖人首出庶物，明足以理〔之〕之至微者，而知有至妙者存，故能盡此宜民之神〔所〕，爲法於天下。巧者能窺測其一，制作於聖人而垂範妙於無窮，此聖以爲大，著龜功用之大於斯亦可見矣。
抑論制器尚象，不世之大功；制度考文，三王之重政。變通之妙以爲天下利者，非聖人之也，所於易之象而後成耳。亦非一人能之，數世數聖人而後備焉。斯人生生之道若此其難，而聖人所以生生斯人若此其勞也。故曰：「如古時無聖人，人之類滅久矣。」信夫！
書
八音克諧，無相奪倫。
translation_en:
…the sage alone, endowed with virtue and position! The wise are certainly adept at inventing things, yet they can accomplish one thing but not another: this is not what constitutes greatness. Only the sage stands above his fellows, with wisdom sufficient to comprehend all things. In the coarsest things he recognizes the presence of the most refined principles; thus he can fully realize the subtleties of adaptation and transformation, bringing benefit to all under Heaven. The wise can approximate his achievement [?]. The skillful are certainly adept at carrying things forward, yet they can suit this but cannot suit this [?]. The wondrous capacity to benefit the people constitutes greatness [?; annotation: “that which”]. Only the sage stands foremost among all beings. His understanding suffices to order even the most minute things [?; annotation: “it/of”], and he recognizes that the most wondrous principles reside within them. Thus he can fully realize this wondrous capacity to benefit the people [annotation: “that which”] and serve as a model for all under Heaven. The skillful can glimpse one aspect of it. Institutions and inventions originate with the sage, whose exemplary patterns extend wondrously without end. This is what makes the sage great [?]; the greatness of the efficacy of “manifesting the tortoise” [?] can also be seen here.
Furthermore, making implements by taking the images as models is an achievement rarely equaled in any age; establishing institutions and examining written forms were major responsibilities of the Three Kings. The subtle workings of adaptation and transformation that benefit all under Heaven are not the sage’s alone [?]: they are accomplished only by drawing upon the images of the Book of Changes [?]. Nor can one person accomplish this: only after several generations and several sages is it complete. So difficult is the way by which these people sustain and perpetuate life, and so arduous are the sages’ labors to sustain and perpetuate their lives. Thus it is said: “Had there been no sages in antiquity, humankind would long since have perished.” How true!
Book of Documents
“The eight kinds of musical sound can be brought into harmony, without any encroaching upon the proper order of the others.”

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
李謨
同考試官訓導張　批〔虞書一題類能言之但分析未明語多重複無愜人意者獨此作融會傳意辭不費而理自足其積學有得者歟〕
同考試官教諭郭　批〔學者童習此題便能口誦今出試多士無那為所窘者惟此作能於克諧無奪倫處挑剔明白而辭氣舂容〕
考試官學正秦　批〔辭理簡暢錄出〕
考試官教授李　批〔得旨〕
〔宛然爲出虞廷樂和氣象宜錄以式來學〕
極其
聖君期樂官者也夫樂以和爲
===
和而不失其倫則和之極矣謂非八聲之
和之所致哉
帝舜命夔典樂教胄子而推言
此
音樂和固所以教人人聲和斯可以
樂之爲音其凡有八若金若石若絲竹
和也今以人聲之和被之而爲樂焉莫不
有所依據自雖雖乎其和鳴若匏土若革木最
難諧也以人聲之和播之而成樂焉莫不有
所憑藉自洋洋乎其諧協翕如純如皦之五味
之相濟何泚瀎之有盡善盡美譬之五色之相
punctuated:
李謨

同考試官訓導張，批〔虞書一題，類能言之，但分析未明，語多重複，無愜人意者。獨此作融會傳意，辭不費而理自足，其積學有得者歟？〕
同考試官教諭郭，批〔學者童習此題，便能口誦。今出試多士，無那為所窘者。惟此作能於克諧無奪倫處挑剔明白，而辭氣舂容。〕
考試官學正秦，批〔辭理簡暢，錄出。〕
考試官教授李，批〔得旨。〕
〔宛然爲出虞廷樂和氣象，宜錄以式來學。〕

極其聖君期樂官者也。夫樂以和爲，和而不失其倫，則和之極矣。謂非八聲之和之所致哉？

帝舜命夔典樂，教胄子，而推言此。音樂和，固所以教人；人聲和，斯可以。樂之爲音，其凡有八，若金若石若絲竹，和也。今以人聲之和被之而爲樂焉，莫不有所依據，自雖雖乎其和鳴。若匏土若革木，最難諧也。以人聲之和播之而成樂焉，莫不有所憑藉，自洋洋乎其諧協。翕如，純如，皦之五味之相濟，何泚瀎之有？盡善盡美，譬之五色之相…
translation_en:
Li Mo

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔On this topic from the Documents of Yu, most candidates could say something, but their analyses were unclear and their language repetitive; none satisfied. This composition alone integrates and conveys the commentary’s meaning: its language is economical, yet its reasoning complete. Surely its author has gained understanding through sustained study?〕
Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor, comments: 〔Students practice this topic in childhood and can readily recite it. Yet now that it has been set for the candidates, many have been troubled by it [?]. This composition alone brings out clearly the meaning of “achieving harmony” and “not disrupting one another’s order,” while its language and tone are ample and unhurried.〕
Examiner Qin, Director of Instruction, comments: 〔Concise and lucid in expression and reasoning. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔It grasps the essential meaning.〕
〔It vividly conveys the atmosphere of musical harmony at the court of Yu [?]. It should be included as a model for future students.〕
Bringing it to its utmost—this is what the sage ruler expected of his music official [?]. Music takes harmony as its …; when it is harmonious without losing its proper order, harmony has reached its utmost. Could this be anything other than the result of the harmony of the eight sounds?

Emperor Shun ordered Kui to direct music and teach the sons of the nobility, and extended his remarks to this. Harmony in music is indeed a means of teaching people; when human voices are harmonious, they can … [?]. The sounds of music comprise eight kinds. Those of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo are harmonious [?]. Now, when the harmony of human voices is imparted to them to make music, each has something on which to rely, and naturally they sound harmoniously together [?]. Those of gourd, clay, hide, and wood are the hardest to harmonize. When the harmony of human voices is diffused through them to make music, each has something on which to depend, and naturally their concord flows abundantly. Together in sound, pure and distinct [?], they are like the five flavors complementing one another: what discord could there be [?]? Perfect in goodness and beauty, they are like the five colors mutually …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
成何促迫之有夫和一於和則和和乖矣羣音並
作之中井然條理之有在初不相侵而失次上
下迭奏　際秩然條貫之自存初不相越而亂
倫脉絡雖貫通也一間一合之惟序陰陽其定
卽奏雖始終也一倡一和之相承晝夜其
□樂之妙如此雖神人亦且和矣而
不可教耶大抵樂本於人心而被於
八音八音既□則八心益有所養而無不和是
之流□也胄子之教執大於是虞廷典
===
格神人舞獸□可謂無愧於聲樂之作而亦無
□非治□曷足以當之哉厥後作樂果能
之命也歟
稽古建官惟百內有百揆四岳外有
州牧侯伯庶政惟和萬國咸寧夏商
官倍亦克用乂明王立政不惟其官
惟其人
曹來聘
同考試官訓導張　批〔措詞简當說理明快　盖嘗究心〕
punctuated:
成，何促迫之有？夫和一於和，則和和乖矣。羣音並作之中，井然條理之有在，初不相侵而失次；上下迭奏際，秩然條貫之自存，初不相越而亂倫。脉絡雖貫通也，一間一合之惟序，陰陽其定；卽奏雖始終也，一倡一和之相承，晝夜其□。樂之妙如此，雖神人亦且和矣，而不可教耶？大抵樂本於人心而被於八音，八音既□，則八心益有所養而無不和。是之流□也。胄子之教，執大於是。虞廷典格神人，舞獸□，可謂無愧於聲樂之作，而亦無□非治□，曷足以當之哉？厥後作樂，果能之命也歟？

稽古建官，惟百。內有百揆、四岳，外有州牧、侯伯。庶政惟和，萬國咸寧。夏商官倍，亦克用乂。明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。

曹來聘

同考試官訓導張批〔措詞简當，說理明快，盖嘗究心〕
translation_en:
…complete one another: what haste or constraint could there be? If harmony consists solely in harmony, then harmony itself goes awry [?]. Amid the simultaneous sounding of the many tones, an orderly arrangement remains; they never encroach upon one another and lose their sequence. As high and low alternate, a coherent order persists; they never overstep one another and disrupt their proper relations. Though their connecting strands run throughout, their alternations of separation and union follow a sequence, establishing yin and yang. Though the performance [?] has a beginning and an end, call and response succeed one another, and day and night … [illegible]. Such is the subtle efficacy of music: even spirits and human beings will be brought into harmony. Could it then fail to educate? Music originates in the human heart and is expressed through the eight classes of musical instruments. Once these eight classes are … [illegible], the “eight hearts” [?] receive still greater nourishment and are all brought into harmony. This is its spreading … [illegible]. In educating the sons of the nobility, the essential principle is grasped here [?]. At the court of Yu, the director of music [?] brought spirits and human beings into accord and made the beasts dance … [illegible]. This could be called worthy of the creation of vocal and instrumental music. Yet there was also no … [illegible]; unless there was order … [illegible], how could one be equal to it [?]? When music was subsequently created, could it indeed fulfill that command [?]?

“Examining antiquity, we find that the offices established numbered only one hundred. Within the court were the Chief Minister and the Four Chiefs; outside were the Regional Governors and the chiefs of the feudal lords. All affairs of government were harmonious, and the myriad states were at peace. Under Xia and Shang, the number of offices doubled, yet they too were able to achieve good order. When an enlightened king establishes government, what matters is not the offices but the men.”

Cao Laipin 曹來聘.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The wording is concise and apt, and the exposition of principles clear and lucid. Evidently he has devoted careful attention …〕

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
於經學者
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔題不甚長而意難收拾此作依傳數去掃陳言之陋作家也本房得士如此良可藉手以〕
獻矣
考試官學正秦　批〔寫出唐虞夏商制治保邦之意〕
試官教授李　批〔明整可誦〕
代建官有其效必指其建官之要也
致治固在於建官建官莫要於得人也古之
聖賢述之以訓官其知本歟且成王
===
謂昔唐虞稽舜之帝天下也仰稽古
建官則惟馬內而百揆四岳總治於王朝
侯伯總治於方岳內外相承體統不
庶政之多或咸熙或其凝無一之不
萬國之廣或時雍或風動無一之不寧也
及至夏商禹湯之王天下也上視唐虞建官則
惟倍治不止於揆岳總之者增其數外治
不止於牧伯總之者加其負會通是觀繁簡以
制故當時大功叙而耿命釐庶政亦惟和也文
punctuated:
於經學者。
同考試官教諭鄭，批〔題不甚長而意難收拾，此作依傳數去掃陳言之陋，作家也。本房得士如此，良可藉手以〕獻矣。
考試官學正秦，批〔寫出唐虞夏商制治保邦之意。〕
試官教授李，批〔明整可誦。〕
代建官有其效，必指其建官之要也。
致治固在於建官，建官莫要於得人也。古之聖賢述之以訓官，其知本歟？且成王謂昔唐虞，稽舜之帝天下也，仰稽古，建官則惟馬。內而百揆、四岳總治於王朝，侯伯總治於方岳，內外相承，體統不。庶政之多，或咸熙，或其凝，無一之不；萬國之廣，或時雍，或風動，無一之不寧也。及至夏商，禹湯之王天下也，上視唐虞，建官則惟倍。治不止於揆岳，總之者增其數；外治不止於牧伯，總之者加其負。會通是觀，繁簡以制，故當時大功叙而耿命釐，庶政亦惟和也。文
translation_en:
…one who has devoted attention to the study of the Classics.
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “The topic is not very long, but its meaning is difficult to encompass. This composition follows the commentary [the following wording is doubtful: 數去] and sweeps away the defects of stale expressions: this is an accomplished writer. For our examining room to have obtained such a scholar gives us something worthy to present.”
Examiner Qin, Director of Studies, comments: “It brings out the intent behind establishing good government and securing the state under Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang.”
Examining official Li, Professor, comments: “Clear and orderly, worthy of recitation.”
The establishment of offices through successive ages [?] had its effects; one must therefore identify the essential principle behind establishing them.
Achieving good government certainly depends upon establishing offices, and nothing is more essential in establishing offices than obtaining the right people. The sages and worthies of antiquity recounted this to instruct officials: did they not understand the root of the matter? Now King Cheng spoke of the ancient ages of Tang and Yu. Examining how Shun ruled All under Heaven as emperor, we find that he looked up to antiquity for his model and established offices numbering only ‘horses’ [?]. Within, the Chief Minister and the Four Mountains directed government at the royal court; the regional lords directed government in the regions. The inner and outer administrations supported one another, and the institutional order did not… [?]. Of the many affairs of government, some flourished universally and others became firmly established; none failed to… [?]. Across the vast array of states, some enjoyed harmony and others responded as if moved by the wind; none was without peace.
When it came to Xia and Shang, and Yu and Tang ruled All under Heaven as kings, they looked back to Tang and Yu but established twice as many offices. Government was no longer confined to the Chief Minister and the Four Mountains: those directing it increased in number. Government outside the capital was no longer confined to regional governors and lords: those directing it took on greater responsibilities. Considering these arrangements comprehensively, they regulated the complexity or simplicity of administration accordingly. Thus, at that time great achievements were duly ordered and the illustrious mandate was put into effect; the many affairs of government were likewise harmonious. The civilizing…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
命敷而兆民殖萬國亦咸寧也是皆歷代建官
之明效如此其要果安在哉蓋唐虞明王之立
政也惟百宣貴官之多耶凡在百之列者
必惟三德六德之翕受也曰俊曰又之敷施也
惡德何有哉夏商明王之立政也建官惟
之冗耶凡在倍之數者必惟曰賢曰
過即宅即俊之克用也官及私昵何
哉是其制而治以至保邦而所以安者如
訓迪可不知所監耶入抵主治者
===
以者臣王既舉外攘之功即嚴内治
脩而拳拳建官也然此歷述唐虞夏商之
前代之宏規成一時之定制下文又
復以為之本焉嗚呼為政在人取人
此成周之治所以不可及也成王其賢矣
哉
詩
天保定爾亦孔之固俾爾單厚何福不除
俾爾多益以莫不庶
punctuated:
命敷而兆民殖，萬國亦咸寧也。是皆歷代建官之明效如此，其要果安在哉？蓋唐虞明王之立政也，惟百，宣貴官之多耶？凡在百之列者，必惟三德六德之翕受也，曰俊曰又之敷施也，惡德何有哉？夏商明王之立政也，建官惟，之冗耶？凡在倍之數者，必惟曰賢曰，過即宅即俊之克用也，官及私昵何哉？是其制而治，以至保邦，而所以安者如。訓迪可不知所監耶？入抵主治者，以者臣王既舉外攘之功，即嚴内治脩，而拳拳建官也。然此歷述唐虞夏商之，前代之宏規，成一時之定制。下文又復以為之本焉。嗚呼！為政在人，取人，此成周之治所以不可及也。成王其賢矣哉！

詩

天保定爾，亦孔之固。俾爾單厚，何福不除？俾爾多益，以莫不庶。
translation_en:
… commands spread and the myriad people flourished; the countless states likewise all enjoyed peace. Such were the manifest results of establishing offices under successive dynasties. Where, then, did the essential principle truly lie? When the enlightened kings of Tang and Yu established their governments, they had only a hundred officials. Did they prize having many officials [?]? All who belonged to that hundred were necessarily accepted for their possession of the three virtues or the six virtues; those called outstanding and those called you [?] were appointed to serve. How could there have been men of evil character among them? When the enlightened kings of Xia and Shang established their governments, they instituted offices … were these excessive [?]? All included in their doubled number were necessarily called worthy and …; they successfully employed those described as settled and outstanding [?]. How could offices have gone to private favorites? Thus their institutions brought order and ultimately preserved their states; this was how peace was secured [?]. In receiving instruction and guidance, could one fail to recognize what should serve as a warning? Those who undertake the governance of the ruler … [?].

… Once the king had accomplished the work of repelling external threats, he strictly attended to internal governance and devoted earnest care to establishing offices [?]. Yet this passage recounts the precedents of Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang, taking the grand patterns of earlier ages to form the settled institutions of its own time [?]. The text below again treats … as their foundation [?]. Ah! Government depends upon people, and the selection of people … [?]. This is why the governance of Zhou in its perfection could not be equaled. How worthy King Cheng was!

Book of Odes

Heaven protects and establishes you, making you very secure. It grants you abundant bounty: what blessing does it not bestow? It grants you ever greater increase, so that nothing fails to flourish.

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
李獻
同考試官訓導汪　批〔人臣頌君舍天福無以爲言此篇體貼出詩人忠愛其君之意是亦有忠愛之心者歟〕
同考試官訓導逯　批〔臣子答君意思正如此子能言之是亦忠愛其君者也尚有驗於他日〕
考試官訓導朱　批〔揭書出題本自平易作者多不玩傳註惟此篇形容詩人答君之意宛然在目錄之〕
考試官學正秦　批〔詞不繁而意自足佳作也〕
考試官教授　批〔理明詞整〕
===
君天眷之至而使之獲福之隆也蓋眷
至而福之臣人君所大欲也臣子言其君之
如此忠愛之意何切哉昔天保臣子
作歌此詩以答之其意謂夫吾君爲
于奉天之道而天之眷之者何如其必蒼
冥之中保之佑之而安定孔堅九重泰然無震
騰也上之表裁之培之而寵綏甚固清穆晏
如無杌隉也于以使之受天之祜弟祿是康渾
淪磅礴而不可以限量窺荷天之休純嘏是常
punctuated:
李獻

同考試官訓導汪　批〔人臣頌君，舍天福無以爲言。此篇體貼出詩人忠愛其君之意，是亦有忠愛之心者歟？〕
同考試官訓導逯　批〔臣子答君，意思正如此。子能言之，是亦忠愛其君者也，尚有驗於他日。〕
考試官訓導朱　批〔揭書出題，本自平易，作者多不玩傳註。惟此篇形容詩人答君之意，宛然在目，錄之。〕
考試官學正秦　批〔詞不繁而意自足，佳作也。〕
考試官教授　批〔理明詞整。〕

君天眷之至，而使之獲福之隆也。蓋眷至而福之臣，人君所大欲也。臣子言其君之如此，忠愛之意何切哉！昔天保，臣子作歌此詩以答之，其意謂夫吾君爲于奉天之道，而天之眷之者何如？其必蒼冥之中，保之佑之，而安定孔堅，九重泰然，無震騰也。上之表，裁之培之，而寵綏甚固，清穆晏如，無杌隉也。于以使之受天之祜，弟祿是康，渾淪磅礴，而不可以限量窺；荷天之休，純嘏是常，
translation_en:
Li Xian 李獻

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: 〔When a subject praises his ruler, he has nothing to speak of apart from Heaven’s blessings. This essay sympathetically brings out the poet’s loyal love for his ruler. Does its author, too, possess a heart of loyal love?〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor: 〔Precisely such should be the sentiments of a subject responding to his ruler. Since you can express them, you too are one who loyally loves his ruler. May this yet be borne out in days to come.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The topic, selected by opening the book, is inherently straightforward, yet most writers fail to ponder the commentaries and annotations. This essay alone portrays the poet’s intention in responding to his ruler so vividly that it seems present before our eyes. I select it for inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Qin, Instructor: 〔The wording is not prolix, yet the meaning is complete in itself. A fine composition.〕
Comment by the Examiner, Professor: 〔Clear reasoning and orderly expression.〕

…Heaven’s regard for the ruler reaches its utmost, enabling him to obtain blessings in abundance [?]. For the utmost regard and the bestowal of blessings [?] are what a ruler greatly desires. When a subject speaks of his ruler in this way, how earnest is his loyal love! In former times, in “Heaven Protects You” (Tian bao), the subjects composed this song in response to their ruler. Its meaning is this: our ruler follows the way of serving Heaven [?]; how, then, does Heaven show its regard for him? Surely, from within the azure heavens, it protects and assists him, making his security exceedingly firm, so that within the ninefold palace all is at ease, without upheaval. Above [?], it nurtures and sustains him, making its favor and protection exceedingly secure, so that all is tranquil, reverent, and peaceful, without peril. Thus it enables him to receive Heaven’s blessings: prosperity and emoluments bring well-being [?], vast and all-encompassing beyond any measure by which they might be fathomed; he receives Heaven’s favor, and great blessings are his constant lot…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
廣大豐裕而不可以涯涘測不惟厚也罔不舊
者將除新者已生休徵相繼綿綿乎其不絕往
者方　　者即續嘉慶頻仍亹亹乎其無窮天
之福君單厚而除也蓋如此且又俾之多福之
者敷錫在加日進於無疆穰穰乎其盛也
行者甲重不已日增於無際簡簡乎
徒盛也莫不羣然畢集如幾如式足
此而充於朝與之俱馬林然駢臻時萬
於內　於外左右與之會馬大之福
===
而燕　如此于托天眷君之至使君
福之隆天　臣　其亦飽君之恩而答稱之
序鹿鳴以下五詩君所以燕其臣天
所以答其君也君之燕臣則極致
歎篤厚之意臣之答君則深願以盛大悠
久之福君燕其臣臣媚其君此所以爲乾之同
聲相　　之上下相交也此有周之所以卒致
𤰞熙泰和之治而爲有道之長也猗歟盛哉
虎拜稽首天子萬年
punctuated:
廣大豐裕，而不可以涯涘測。不惟厚也，罔不舊者將除，新者已生，休徵相繼，綿綿乎其不絕；往者方　　者即續，嘉慶頻仍，亹亹乎其無窮。天之福君，單厚而除也，蓋如此。且又俾之多福之者，敷錫在加，日進於無疆，穰穰乎其盛也。行者甲重不已，日增於無際，簡簡乎。徒盛也，莫不羣然畢集，如幾如式，足此而充於朝，與之俱馬；林然駢臻，時萬於內　於外，左右與之會馬。大之福而燕　如此，于托天眷君之至，使君福之隆，天　臣　其亦飽君之恩而答稱之。
序《鹿鳴》以下五詩，君所以燕其臣，天所以答其君也。君之燕臣，則極致歎篤厚之意；臣之答君，則深願以盛大悠久之福。君燕其臣，臣媚其君，此所以爲乾之同聲相　　之上下相交也。此有周之所以卒致𤰞熙泰和之治，而爲有道之長也。猗歟，盛哉！虎拜稽首，天子萬年！
translation_en:
…vast and abundant, beyond the measure of any bounds. Nor are these blessings merely generous: as the old are about to pass away, new ones have already arisen. Auspicious signs follow one another in an unbroken succession. As those departing are just … others immediately continue [?]; fortunate blessings recur repeatedly, proceeding tirelessly without end. Such indeed is Heaven’s blessing of the ruler, abundant and renewed [?]. Furthermore, it grants him many blessings, bestowing ever more, daily extending them without limit: how richly abundant they are! What follows accumulates without cease [?], increasing daily without bounds, magnificent indeed. [The following passage is badly garbled.] They all assemble together; “like … like …” [?], filling the court and accompanying him [?]. They arrive together in dense ranks, … within … without; those on the left and right gather with him [?]. So great are the blessings and the repose … [?]. This expresses the utmost of Heaven’s solicitude for the ruler and the fullness of the ruler’s blessings [?]. … The ministers, too, have received their fill of the ruler’s favor and respond with praise [?].
The preface states that “The Deer Call” (Lu ming) and the following five poems concern the ruler’s feasting of his ministers; “Heaven …” is the means of answering their ruler [?]. When the ruler feasts his ministers, he fully expresses his profound and generous affection [?]; when the ministers answer their ruler, they earnestly wish him blessings both abundant and enduring. The ruler feasts his ministers, and the ministers love their ruler. Thus … voices respond in harmony … and those above and below enter into mutual communion [?]. This is how the Zhou ultimately achieved a flourishing, peaceful, and harmonious government [?] and became foremost among those possessing the Way. Ah, how glorious! Hu bows and knocks his head to the ground: “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!”

至敬以□君賜，致祝以謝乎君恩。夫君固當致敬□受之也，然非祝之以壽考，則□報謝之私哉？詩人美召虎平淮南之功命如此，意謂惟召虎建平夷之大，我周輿□功之盛典。恩命既頒於殿陛，策書遂錫於岐周。虎之於此，展拜于文祖賞功之廟，稽首仰策命，如仰天顏也；行禮于召祖受命之所，稽顙翼翼，對策書，如對斧扆也。若圭瓚，若秬鬯，辰章烜赫，欽受於俯伏之時，肅乎恭
translation_en:
Zhao Jiying.

Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He expresses a subject’s desire to repay and thank his ruler within the proper bounds of literary composition. A fine scholar.”
Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The solemn intention to revere the ruler and wish him blessings is developed almost exhaustively. Here, too, is someone skilled in explaining the Poetry.”
Associate Examiner Zhu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The old compositions [?] are all excellent, but this particular essay conveys the ancients’ love for their ruler, leaving almost nothing unexpressed. Finding this made me leap with delight. Who but you could rank first in the Poetry examination section?”
Examiner Qin, Instructor, comments: “Pure and correct in its □; recorded as a model for those who follow.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”

With utmost reverence, [□] the ruler’s gifts; offer wishes for his blessings to thank him for his grace. Indeed, one should receive the ruler’s [gifts] with reverence [□]. Yet without wishing him longevity, how could one [□] one’s personal desire to repay and thank him? Thus the poet praises the achievement of Shao Hu in pacifying Huainan and the command rewarding him. The meaning is that Shao Hu accomplished the great work of pacifying the Yi, and our Zhou held a grand ceremony for [rewarding?] his achievement. Once the gracious command had been promulgated at the palace steps, the written investiture was bestowed at Qizhou. Thereupon Hu bowed in the temple of the cultivated ancestor, where meritorious service was rewarded. Touching his head to the ground, he looked up toward the investiture document as though looking up at the imperial countenance. He performed the rites at the place where the ancestor of Shao had received his appointment. Reverently striking his forehead upon the ground, he faced the written command as though facing the axe-patterned screen behind the sovereign’s throne. Such gifts as the jade-handled libation ladle and the black-millet sacrificial wine, with their resplendent insignia [?], he reverently received while prostrate, solemn in his reverence…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
敬之匪懈若山川若土田睿藻輝煌敬承於舞
□□之際凛乎戒慎之靡寧當斯之時虎也感君
恩之
□□如天之高也果將何以爲報乎荷寵
命之隆重如地之厚也抑將何以爲謝乎惟願
□□子君壽萬年荷天和以康强黄其髮台
□□□中興之景運萬年如一日也勉勉
以鎮再造
□□崇享遐齡而吉慶昌而大耆而艾
□□洪□萬載如一時也吁君之報
□殊當之臣之報謝而致無窮之祝盛
===
□可謂□施報之道矣抑又論之召公
淮南之夷□宣二舉報功之典固禮也然必
□□峻周從其祖康公受命於文王之
□□者何哉蓋國莫重於世臣而臣莫
□功故耳宣王平淮南而有召虎之爲將
伐淮北而得皇父之治師其所以能致中興之
盛者□賴此世臣之助也哉
春秋
公伐齊納糾　齊小白入於齊　莊公九年
punctuated:
敬之匪懈。若山川，若土田，睿藻輝煌，敬承於舞□□之際，凛乎戒慎之靡寧。當斯之時，虎也感君恩之□□如天之高也，果將何以爲報乎？荷寵命之隆重如地之厚也，抑將何以爲謝乎？惟願□□子君壽萬年，荷天和以康强，黄其髮，台□□□中興之景運，萬年如一日也；勉勉以鎮再造，□□崇享遐齡，而吉慶昌而大，耆而艾，□□洪□，萬載如一時也。吁！君之報□殊當之，臣之報謝而致無窮之祝，盛□可謂□施報之道矣。抑又論之，召公淮南之夷□宣二舉報功之典，固禮也。然必□□峻周，從其祖康公受命於文王之□□者，何哉？蓋國莫重於世臣，而臣莫□功故耳。宣王平淮南而有召虎之爲將，伐淮北而得皇父之治師，其所以能致中興之盛者，□賴此世臣之助也哉！

春秋

公伐齊納糾，齊小白入於齊。莊公九年。
translation_en:
…respectful and unremitting. As for the mountains and rivers, the lands and fields, the royal composition shone brilliantly. Respectfully receiving it while performing the ceremonial dance [?], he remained solemnly vigilant, never at ease. At that moment, Hu felt his ruler’s favor to be [?] as lofty as Heaven: how indeed could he repay it? Bearing the weight of an august command as substantial as the earth, how could he express his thanks? He could only wish that his lord [?] might live ten thousand years, receiving Heaven’s harmony to remain healthy and strong, his hair turning yellow with age [?]; that the glorious fortunes of the restoration might endure for ten thousand years as for a single day; and that, striving unceasingly, he might secure the renewed dynasty, [?] enjoy a long life, and see his blessings flourish and increase. Growing old and venerable, [?], may ten thousand years be as a single moment! Ah! The ruler’s recompense [?] was exceptionally fitting; the subject expressed his gratitude through wishes without end. Such magnificence [?] may be said to embody the way of giving and requital.

Yet let us consider this further. In connection with Lord Shao’s pacification of Huainan, [?] the ceremony of rewarding merit was indeed in accordance with ritual. But why was it necessary to [?] Zhou and follow the precedent of his ancestor, Duke Kang, receiving commands from King Wen [?]? It was because nothing is more important to a state than its hereditary ministers, and for a minister nothing [?] merit. When King Xuan pacified Huainan, he had Shao Hu as his general; when he attacked Huaibei, he obtained Huangfu to marshal his army. Was not his ability to achieve the flourishing restoration dependent [?] upon the assistance of these hereditary ministers?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The duke attacked Qi to install Jiu. Xiaobai of Qi entered Qi.” Ninth year of Duke Zhuang.

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人謂其傷勇而以自經溝瀆賤之也不然則
忍之節義傳播於天下矣春秋書伐齊納糾而
不書　而明糾之不當立也以此若小白亦襄
公之庶子當出奔於莒矣一旦駕反國之轅自
以立其位焉當斯際也莒之力孤而弱
□强輒乃據國以入可謂難矣且內
无君上不禀命於天子王法所宜絕
然立庶以　大　之達道小白乃子糾之兄
傳謂□　所固有也位其所宜居也噫
===
行□□□□幾哉正名乎此官仲輔相桓
聖人謂其　義而以一匡天下稱之也不然
暴白於當世矣春秋雖不稱公子
者明小白之當立也以此吁兄弟
幼之節有一定不可易之理春秋譏子
糾而予桓公其意深矣雖然子糾固不足論矣
然小　　於糾尤有可議者仁人之於弟也不
藏怒焉不宿怨焉親愛之而已矣糾雖爭立越
在他國置而不問可也必請于魯殺之然後快
punctuated: 聖人謂其傷勇，而以自經溝瀆賤之也。不然，則忍之節義傳播於天下矣。春秋書伐齊納糾，而不書　，而明糾之不當立也。以此，若小白亦襄公之庶子，當出奔於莒矣。一旦駕反國之轅，自以立其位焉。當斯際也，莒之力孤而弱，□强輒乃據國以入，可謂難矣。且內无君，上不禀命於天子，王法所宜絕。然立庶以　大　之達道，小白乃子糾之兄。傳謂□　所固有也，位其所宜居也。噫！行□□□□幾哉！正名乎此，官仲輔相桓，聖人謂其　義，而以一匡天下稱之也。不然，暴白於當世矣。春秋雖不稱公子，者明小白之當立也。以此，吁！兄弟幼之節，有一定不可易之理。春秋譏子糾而予桓公，其意深矣。雖然，子糾固不足論矣。然小　　於糾，尤有可議者。仁人之於弟也，不藏怒焉，不宿怨焉，親愛之而已矣。糾雖爭立，越在他國，置而不問可也。必請于魯殺之，然後快
translation_en: …The Sage called it injurious courage [?] and disparaged it as hanging oneself in a ditch. Otherwise, such forbearance and integrity [?] would have been proclaimed throughout the world. The Spring and Autumn Annals records “attacked Qi to install Jiu,” but does not write [text missing], thereby making clear that Jiu ought not to have been installed. On this basis [?], Xiaobai, likewise a son of Duke Xiang by a secondary consort, had fled to Ju. Then one day he turned his carriage homeward and undertook to establish himself in that position. At this juncture, Ju was isolated and weak; [illegible] strong, he thereupon occupied the state and entered it [?]—something that could indeed be called difficult. Moreover, there was no ruler within the state, and he had received no command from the Son of Heaven above: royal law ought to have excluded him. Yet in installing a son of a secondary consort, the universal principle is to [text defective; apparently concerning seniority]. Xiaobai was Zijiu’s elder brother. The Commentary says [illegible]: it was inherently his, and the position was one he ought to occupy. Alas! Conduct [four illegible characters]—how nearly so [?]! Here the names and statuses are rectified. Guan Zhong [transcribed 官仲] assisted Duke Huan; the Sage called his conduct righteous [text defective] and praised him for bringing all under Heaven into order. Otherwise, [something] would have been plainly exposed to his contemporaries. Although the Spring and Autumn Annals does not call him “ducal son,” [text defective] this makes clear that Xiaobai ought to have been installed. On this basis—ah!—the distinctions between brothers and their relative ages [text defective] have a fixed principle that cannot be altered. The Spring and Autumn Annals censures Zijiu and approves Duke Huan: its meaning is profound. Even so, Zijiu scarcely merits further discussion. Yet in Xiao[bai]’s treatment of Jiu [text defective], there is something especially open to criticism. A humane person neither harbors anger nor nurses resentment against his younger brother; he simply cherishes and loves him. Although Jiu had contested the succession, he was away in another state. It would have been enough to leave him alone. To insist on asking Lu to kill him, and only then feel satisfied…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
王尚志
〔指書出題本自平易場屋中多騁浮詞殊失輕重晚閱此卷體貼親切其逐於麟經者乎宜錄出之以矯時習〕
同考試官訓導王　批
〔說出春秋正名分之意〕
考試官學正秦　批
〔春秋以天理裁世事此作得〕
試官教授李　批
國者著人心不附而明其不當立於
國者著王法不容而明其所當立此子糾特
曰不書子白不書公子而繫之齊也春
===
秋定分之謹何其嚴哉昔齊襄遭禍國嗣
未定有如子糾乃襄公之庶子嘗出奔於魯矣
魯之心自魯伐齊而欲奪其位焉當
時管召爲之輔外有魯莊爲之援宜
國以聽莫之拒也然羣臣異向而不以爲
君百姓共疾而不以爲主人心已不附矣且弟
不先　今之通義糾乃小白之弟又未嘗爲
世子國非其所宜有也位非其所宜居也噫非
其有而有之不幾於亂倫乎此召忽致身子糾
punctuated:
王尚志
〔指書出題，本自平易，場屋中多騁浮詞，殊失輕重。晚閱此卷，體貼親切，其逐於麟經者乎？宜錄出之，以矯時習。〕
同考試官訓導王　批：〔說出春秋正名分之意。〕
考試官學正秦　批：〔春秋以天理裁世事，此作得。〕
試官教授李　批

國者，著人心不附而明其不當立；於國者，著王法不容而明其所當立。此子糾特曰不書子，白不書公子而繫之齊也。春秋定分之謹，何其嚴哉！昔齊襄遭禍，國嗣未定。有如子糾，乃襄公之庶子，嘗出奔於魯矣。魯之心，自魯伐齊而欲奪其位焉。當時管召爲之輔，外有魯莊爲之援，宜國以聽，莫之拒也。然羣臣異向而不以爲君，百姓共疾而不以爲主，人心已不附矣。且弟不先　今之通義，糾乃小白之弟，又未嘗爲世子，國非其所宜有也，位非其所宜居也。噫！非其有而有之，不幾於亂倫乎？此召忽致身子糾

Wang Shangzhi
〔The question, drawn directly from the book, was originally straightforward. In the examination hall, however, many indulged in empty rhetoric, badly misjudging what deserved emphasis. Reading this script late in the proceedings, I found its interpretation closely attuned to the text. Might it be pursuing the meaning of the Classic of the Qilin—the Spring and Autumn Annals[?]? It should be selected for inclusion to correct contemporary habits.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: 〔It brings out the Spring and Autumn Annals’ intention of rectifying names and statuses.〕
Comment by Examiner Qin, Instructor (xuezheng): 〔The Spring and Autumn Annals judges worldly affairs by Heaven’s principles. This composition grasps this[?].〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor (jiaoshou).

… the state: this reveals that the people’s hearts did not adhere to him and makes clear that he ought not to have been enthroned. … in the state: this reveals what royal law would not permit and makes clear who ought to have been enthroned[?]. Thus, concerning Zijiu, it specifically says that zi is not written[?]; concerning Bai, it does not write “ducal son,” but associates him with Qi. How rigorous the Spring and Autumn Annals is in carefully determining rightful status!

Formerly, when Duke Xiang of Qi met with disaster, succession to the state was unsettled. Zijiu, for example, was Duke Xiang’s son by a concubine and had fled to Lu. Lu’s intention, in attacking Qi from Lu, was to seize the position for him[?]. At that time, Guan and Shao assisted him, while externally Duke Zhuang of Lu supported him. One might have expected the state to obey, with no one resisting. Yet the ministers favored someone else and would not regard him as their ruler; the common people shared an aversion to him and would not regard him as their lord. The people’s hearts already withheld their allegiance.

Moreover, that a younger brother should not take precedence … is a generally accepted principle of the present day[?]. Jiu was Xiaobai’s younger brother and had never been heir apparent. The state was not rightfully his to possess, nor was the throne rightfully his to occupy. Alas! To possess what is not rightfully one’s own—is this not close to throwing familial order into confusion? In this, Shao Hu devoted himself to Zijiu …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
既歸往請于晉大舉召陵之師焉斯時也孰不
曰晉主夏盟中國所仰若嘉穀之望雨也安夏
攘夷其職耳夫何荀寅之貨未得蔡侯之請
遂辭假以水潦方降聊爲淺事之侵托以中山
□下□師之令上焉徒勤天子之元老下
□之諸侯勢雖足以有爲而心則沮
利者人欲之私今晉定惟利是求而
安攘之功□此雖無專命之愆其事何足算
□□□□之役不書伐而書侵者所以
===
也□□□不於是而衰乎自是以往楚
無忌長惡以不悛興師以圍蔡於是蔡侯莫
矣遂興柏舉之師焉斯時也孰不曰
天下莫强豈諸侯所能以爭救災恤
□望也女而從蔡侯之請仲簡書之義舍
□□撲楚焰於方張振旅漢陽拯蔡危於既
溺上以達天子之命下有以成伯討之功心
雖出於不誠而事則適於義矣噫義者天理之
公今闔閭恃義是從而成安攘之功如此雖無
punctuated:
既歸，往請于晉，大舉召陵之師焉。斯時也，孰不曰：晉主夏盟，中國所仰，若嘉穀之望雨也。安夏攘夷，其職耳。夫何荀寅之貨未得，蔡侯之請遂辭，假以水潦方降，聊爲淺事之侵，托以中山□下□師之令。上焉徒勤天子之元老，下□之諸侯，勢雖足以有爲，而心則沮。利者，人欲之私。今晉定惟利是求，而安攘之功□，此雖無專命之愆，其事何足算？□□□□之役，不書伐而書侵者，所以也。□□□不於是而衰乎？
自是以往，楚無忌，長惡以不悛，興師以圍蔡。於是蔡侯莫矣，遂興柏舉之師焉。斯時也，孰不曰：天下莫强，豈諸侯所能以爭？救災恤□，望也。女而從蔡侯之請，仲簡書之義，舍□□，撲楚焰於方張，振旅漢陽，拯蔡危於既溺。上以達天子之命，下有以成伯討之功。心雖出於不誠，而事則適於義矣。噫！義者，天理之公。今闔閭恃義是從，而成安攘之功如此，雖無
translation_en:
…after returning, [the Marquis of Cai] went to request aid from Jin, and a great army was mobilized at Shaoling. At that time, who would not have said: “Jin presides over the covenant of the Chinese states. The central states look up to it as fine grain longs for rain. Securing the Chinese states and repelling the barbarians are its proper duties.” Yet because Xun Yin did not obtain the goods he demanded, the Marquis of Cai’s request was rejected. Using the onset of flooding as an excuse, Jin undertook only a limited incursion, invoking Zhongshan and an order concerning the army [?]. Above, it merely wearied the Son of Heaven’s senior minister; below, [the text concerning] the feudal lords is damaged [?]. Though its power was sufficient to accomplish something, its resolve was thwarted. Profit represents the selfishness of human desire. Now Duke Ding of Jin sought profit alone, while his achievement in securing the Chinese states and repelling the barbarians [is illegible]. Even if he committed no offense of issuing commands on his own authority, how could his undertaking count for anything? This is why, for the campaign of [four illegible characters], the Spring and Autumn Annals records an “incursion” rather than a “punitive expedition” [?]. Did not […] decline at this point?
From then onward, Chu acted without restraint, persisting in evil without reform, and raised an army to besiege Cai. At this, the Marquis of Cai [was left without recourse?], and the army for the campaign at Boju was consequently raised. At that time, who would not have said: “None under Heaven is stronger. How could the feudal lords contend with it? Relief from calamity and assistance in […] are what is hoped for [?].” Yet [Wu?] acceded to the Marquis of Cai’s request, [upholding?] the duty expressed in the written commands, and setting aside […] [?], quenched Chu’s blaze just as it was flaring up. It marshaled its troops north of the Han River and rescued Cai from peril when it was already drowning. Above, it carried out the Son of Heaven’s command; below, it achieved the merit of a hegemon’s punitive campaign. Though its intentions were insincere, its actions accorded with righteousness. Ah! Righteousness is the impartiality of Heaven’s principle. Now Helü relied upon righteousness and followed it, accomplishing so much in securing the Chinese states and repelling the barbarians, even though he lacked…

translation_en:
…although he lacked a genuine concern for others’ distress, was this deed not nevertheless good? Thus, in recording the battle of Boju, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not use his state’s designation but calls him “Viscount,” thereby commending him. The culpability of Jin’s hegemon—if not here, then □□ [?]. Thus, appealing to Jin was as difficult as that, while appealing to Wu was as easy as this. What should have been easy proved difficult, and what should have been difficult proved easy; their respective merits and failings are surely clear [?]. Nevertheless, the disgraceful conduct at Shaoling scarcely merits discussion. As for Boju, although □□□, was it an act of rescue [?]? The rescue was indeed great. Helü, Zixu, and Grand Steward Pi all harbored □□; when □ went to request assistance, the appeal happened to suit their purposes [?]. They had no genuine commitment to rescuing those in calamity, aiding neighboring states, or fulfilling the obligations of written covenants among the central states [?]. The Sage’s Way was great and his virtue broad; he gladly allowed others □□□□, commending and advancing them for their goodness [?]. Hence his manner of recording the event was as it was.
Record of Rites
“Thus Heaven □ rain and moisture, and the gentleman comprehends its unceasing activity.”
Examiner Qin, School Instructor, comments: 〔Many have failed to grasp correctly the words ‘unceasing activity’ in this topic. Some take them to refer to learning □; some interpret them as referring to government; still others take them to refer exclusively to sacrificial repayment. Their confused and jumbled explanations are tiresome to read. This essay〕〔explains the principles thoroughly and clearly, and its wording is ample and well ordered. It may serve as a model, and is therefore included.〕
Zhang Chuan
□ Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔The composition rests on principle and avoids the fault of vague and cursory treatment.〕
Heaven above exercises its power to bring forth and mature material goods; the gentleman apprehends the subtle workings of this ceaseless generation and maturation. This is the origin of the sacrificial institutions [?]. How greatly rain and moisture contribute to material goods!

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
君子悟其妙而達其生成之無已安得不致其
報本之誠乎記祭禮而推原其由謂夫祭有輕
重皆□財物是祭祀固因財物以致義君子則
因雨澤而達理時而春也物皆萌動非雨無以
□彼茲者天油然作雲霈霈之澤由高及
□□□也時而夏也物皆長養非雨無
□□□上帝沛然下雨霶霈之澤由近
遠既露而□是也瑞靄瀰布於兩間庶類自
熙□□□之不被其澤耶和氣絪緼於
===
□□□□勃勃何一物之不蒙其濡耶
時雨澤□□君子之達之也何如哉蓋必即
□微於彼大化橐籥之理而因有以默
□事可知其道於彼大造流行之妙
□□洞察其幾微仰而觀焉則曰大哉乾

punctuated: 君子悟其妙而達其生成之無已，安得不致其報本之誠乎？記祭禮而推原其由，謂夫祭有輕重，皆□財物。是祭祀固因財物以致義，君子則因雨澤而達理。時而春也，物皆萌動，非雨無以□彼。茲者天油然作雲，霈霈之澤由高及□□□也。時而夏也，物皆長養，非雨無□□□。上帝沛然下雨，霶霈之澤由近遠，既露而□是也。瑞靄瀰布於兩間，庶類自熙，□□□之不被其澤耶？和氣絪緼於□□□□，勃勃，何一物之不蒙其濡耶？時雨澤□□，君子之達之也何如哉？蓋必即□微於彼大化橐籥之理，而因有以默□，事可知其道於彼大造流行之妙，□□洞察其幾微。仰而觀焉，則曰：「大哉乾元，□□物資始！」資始之功，亘萬古勉勉而不已也。俯而□□，則曰：「至哉坤元，萬物資生！」資生之功，歷萬世亹亹而不息也。夫知天道不已之功，則用財物以祀天，而凡日月皆在所祭矣。知地道
translation_en: …When the gentleman comprehends its subtle workings and understands that its generation and nurture never cease, how could he fail to offer his sincere gratitude to the source? In recording sacrificial rites and tracing their origins, the text says that sacrifices differ in importance, but all [an illegible character] goods and resources. Thus sacrifices employ goods and resources to give expression to what is right, while the gentleman apprehends principle through the blessings of rain. When the season is spring, all things begin to sprout; without rain there would be no means to [nurture?] them. Now Heaven sends clouds billowing forth, and abundant moisture extends from on high to [illegible]. When the season is summer, all things grow and are nourished; without rain [the text is damaged]. The Lord on High sends down copious rain; its abundant moisture reaches near and far, and, having appeared as dew, [the remainder is doubtful]. Auspicious mist spreads between Heaven and Earth, and the myriad kinds flourish of themselves. [What could fail?] to receive its blessings? Harmonious vital energy intermingles amid [illegible], burgeoning forth: what single thing does not receive its moisture? The blessings of seasonable rain [the text is damaged]—how does the gentleman understand them? Surely he must [discern the subtle workings?] in the principle by which the great transforming process operates like a bellows, and thereby silently [comprehend?] it. Through its workings he can understand its Way in the wondrous circulation of the great creative process [the syntax is doubtful], and [illegible] perceive its subtlest incipient movements. Looking upward, he says: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian, [from which the myriad?] things take their beginning!” Its work of providing beginnings has continued through all antiquity, striving without cease. Looking downward [the text is damaged], he says: “Supreme indeed is the primal power of Kun, from which the myriad things receive life!” Its work of giving life continues through ten thousand generations, tirelessly and without rest. Now, understanding the unceasing work of the Way of Heaven, one uses goods and resources to sacrifice to Heaven, and the sun and moon are both included among the recipients of sacrifice. Understanding the Way of Earth…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
鄉飲酒義其旨如此謂夫鄉飲之禮匪直所以
將禮文實乃所以安人國也彼坐立有序俎豆
有數之行也固如是民之得於觀感者入而
□也孝以事親而發言舉足之不忘弟以事兄
□□隨行之匪懈出而外也隆之以禮而於
□安之以道而於老者養之周民之
□此其知科條方設施也仁讓之教即
然而大興不一詐愚苦怯者無有矣模範方
也□□□即倏然而振舉求一㬥弱暴
===
無□□化之行也又如此由是國其有不
乎合見自山自東環一邦而托處者莫不遵
何仰於彝倫攸叙之日所謂人人有君
□□之禍不作何安如之邪自南自
國□□聚者莫不會極歸極優游於五
見從之久所謂比屋有可封之俗而叛背之
□□何安似之邪吁鄉飲之禮所以感人心
而馴致於化行國安如此此先王所以務重之
而不敢忽歟抑論民心無常從違靡定以禮服
punctuated: 鄉飲酒義，其旨如此。謂夫鄉飲之禮，匪直所以將禮文，實乃所以安人國也。彼坐立有序，俎豆有數之行也，固如是。民之得於觀感者，入而□也，孝以事親，而發言舉足之不忘；弟以事兄，□□隨行之匪懈。出而外也，隆之以禮，而於□；安之以道，而於老者養之周。民之□此，其知科條方設施也，仁讓之教即然而大興，不一詐愚苦怯者無有矣。模範方也，□□□即倏然而振舉，求一㬥弱暴，無□□。化之行也，又如此。由是，國其有不乎？合見自山自東，環一邦而托處者，莫不遵何，仰於彝倫攸叙之日。所謂人人有君，□□之禍不作，何安如之邪？自南自，國□□聚者，莫不會極歸極，優游於五見從之久。所謂比屋有可封之俗，而叛背之□□，何安似之邪？吁！鄉飲之禮，所以感人心，而馴致於化行國安如此。此先王所以務重之，而不敢忽歟？抑論民心無常，從違靡定，以禮服
translation_en:
…the “Meaning of the Village Drinking Ceremony”: such is its purport. The village drinking ceremony does not merely serve to carry out ritual forms; it truly serves to bring peace to a ruler’s state. In its performance, sitting and standing follow an established order, and the sacrificial stands and vessels have prescribed numbers. Such are its arrangements. What the people gain through observing it and being moved by it is this: within the home [?], they serve their parents with filial devotion, never forgetting it in their words or movements; they serve their elder brothers with fraternal deference, remaining diligent in accompanying them [?]. Outside the home, they honor others through ritual propriety [?], provide ease in accordance with the Way, and care fully for the aged. The people’s [illegible] this [?]. Just as the regulations are put into practice, the teaching of benevolence and deference flourishes greatly; not one deceitful, foolish, distressed, or timid person remains [?]. Just as the exemplary standards [are established?], [illegible] are suddenly stirred into action. Seek even one instance of violence against the weak [?], and none [illegible] can be found. Such, too, is the spread of moral transformation.

With this, could the state fail to [enjoy peace?]? We see that those who come from the mountains and from the east [?], dwelling throughout the state, all follow [the norms?], looking up to a time when the enduring human relationships are properly ordered. This is what is meant by everyone acknowledging a ruler: the calamity of [illegible] does not arise. What peace could equal this? From the south and from [missing direction], those who gather within the state [?] all converge upon and turn toward the supreme standard, dwelling at ease for long amid the five [relationships?; text corrupt]. This is what is meant by a society in which every household contains someone worthy of enfeoffment, while rebellion and betrayal [illegible]. What peace could compare with this?

Ah! Such is the way the village drinking ceremony moves people’s hearts and gradually brings about the spread of moral transformation and the peace of the state. Is this not why the former kings made a point of valuing it and dared not neglect it? Furthermore, people’s hearts are inconstant; their obedience and disobedience are unsettled. If one brings them into submission through ritual propriety…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
則效順以勢迫則背馳故先王制爲禮教以防
範之如鄉飲之禮一舉貴賤以明隆殺以辨和
樂不□弟長無遺安燕不亂不特足以正身也
□安國安天下皆係於此焉其有益於世道也
□哉故孔子曰吾觀於鄉而知王道之易易
□□
===
論
學□□成
同考試官訓導王　批　〔五峯此語本自中庸印聚〕
劉啓東
〔張說宋儒之言用唐人之句發中庸之理不失當〕

考試官學正秦　批　〔此論有源委有波瀾有歸〕
〔宿如大河之水發源崑崙千里不息而懸注於海彼行潦無〕
〔源安能彷彿其萬一耶〕

punctuated:
則效順，以勢迫則背馳。故先王制爲禮教以防範之。如鄉飲之禮，一舉貴賤以明，隆殺以辨，和樂不□，弟長無遺，安燕不亂，不特足以正身也。□安國、安天下，皆係於此焉。其有益於世道也，□哉！故孔子曰：「吾觀於鄉，而知王道之易易□□。」

論
學□□成
同考試官訓導王　批　〔五峯此語本自中庸印聚〕

In the village drinking ceremony, a single performance makes distinctions between noble and lowly clear and differentiates degrees of ceremonial honor. Harmonious enjoyment does not [illegible]; deference to elders is never neglected; peaceful conviviality does not lapse into disorder. This is sufficient not merely to rectify oneself. title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
君子之學非務爲大也率吾之本自大也
吾本□大者非私也固天之所以命於我
入之所以託於我也天之命於我也其
分爲□足而其託於我也其任爲甚重吾
□有以副其重與足者而後可也天固足
□歟之天固重之吾固輕之是自小
□渠也豈善繼善述善事其天者哉此
君子之□不屑於小用不苟於小成必責
□□□大□之域而後止者蓋必有以自
===
□□□不□不□其有也彼挾一長持一
□以自□□其學者豈吾所謂學哉吾所謂
□其亦異乎世之學也世凡言學者虛
□之效權謀術數之習諸子百家之
□不列儒科者吾無論矣若夫遊儒者之
門讀□者之書華言而華服繩趨而尺步
非所謂學耶詢其所以學者尋章摘句
摭華鈎奇剽竊陳言以爲富記誦隱僻以
爲博□皆網利媒祿之計固不足以名吾
punctuated:
君子之學，非務爲大也，率吾之本自大也。吾本□大者，非私也，固天之所以命於我，入之所以託於我也。天之命於我也，其分爲□足；而其託於我也，其任爲甚重。吾□有以副其重與足者，而後可也。天固足□歟之，天固重之，吾固輕之，是自小□渠也，豈善繼善述、善事其天者哉？此君子之□，不屑於小用，不苟於小成，必責□□□大□之域而後止者，蓋必有以自□□□不□不□其有也。彼挾一長、持一□以自□□其學者，豈吾所謂學哉？吾所謂□，其亦異乎世之學也。

世凡言學者，虛□之效，權謀術數之習，諸子百家之□，不列儒科者，吾無論矣。若夫遊儒者之門，讀□者之書，華言而華服，繩趨而尺步，非所謂學耶？詢其所以學者，尋章摘句，摭華鈎奇，剽竊陳言以爲富，記誦隱僻以爲博，□皆網利媒祿之計，固不足以名吾
translation_en:
The gentleman’s learning does not strive to be great; in following what is fundamental within us, it is great of itself. The greatness inherent in us [?] is no private possession: it is what Heaven has ordained for me and what has been entrusted to me [the transcription here is doubtful]. In what Heaven ordains for me, my allotted portion is ample [?]; in what it entrusts to me, my responsibility is very heavy. Only when I can measure up to that weight and that abundance [?] will I have done enough. Heaven has indeed made it ample [following words unclear]; Heaven indeed treats it as weighty, yet I treat it lightly. This is to belittle oneself [?]. How could this be faithfully carrying on and fulfilling what has been handed down, or serving one’s Heaven well? Thus the gentleman’s [?] disdains petty employment and does not settle carelessly for small accomplishments, insisting on reaching the realm of greatness [?] before stopping. Surely he must thereby [several characters illegible] what he possesses [?]. Those who rely on a single strength and hold to a single [?], using these to [illegible] their learning—how could theirs be what I call learning? What I call learning [?] is indeed different from the learning of the world.

Among what people commonly call learning, there are the results of empty [?], the practice of schemes and manipulative techniques, and the [?] of the various masters and Hundred Schools. I shall not discuss those that fall outside the Confucian disciplines. But consider those who frequent the gates of Confucian scholars and read the books of [?], whose speech and clothing are ornate, whose movements conform to a cord and whose steps conform to a rule: is this not what is called learning? Ask what their learning consists in: searching out passages and extracting phrases, gathering elegant expressions and fishing for curiosities, plagiarizing stale sayings to appear richly furnished, and memorizing obscure material to appear broadly learned. These are all [?] schemes for netting profit and securing official emoluments. They are certainly insufficient to deserve the name of my …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
學也右乃自立一家之文欲馳聲於翰墨
窮箋一經之註欲寄籍於名流茲二氏者
□規規利祿之學固不類矣然汲汲於名
者亦以汲汲於利也天之所以命我託我者
□在茲邪天之命與託者果不在茲君子
□詎止於茲邪然則君子之學果何
□形於上者天也形於下者地也命於
□間者人也三才鼎立中有仁義道德之
□□之□文物禮樂之具是謂天
===
□□天以清地得以寧人得以安者
□天之□是人也必命之心以涵天下之
□之身以負天下之極命之耳目口以
□言天下之極人必盡極然後可
□俯仰無怍然則天之命我者大邪小邪
然所以命我者又必有以託於我也天不
□清地不能自寧人物不能自安必俟
夫能盡此極者付以參贊之責然則天之
託我者小邪大邪斯命也斯託也惟聖人
punctuated: 學也。右乃自立一家之文，欲馳聲於翰墨；窮箋一經之註，欲寄籍於名流。茲二氏者，□規規利祿之學固不類矣，然汲汲於名者，亦以汲汲於利也。天之所以命我託我者，□在茲邪？天之命與託者果不在茲，君子□詎止於茲邪？然則君子之學果何□？形於上者，天也；形於下者，地也；命於□間者，人也。三才鼎立，中有仁義道德之□□之□，文物禮樂之具，是謂天□□。天以清，地得以寧，人得以安者，□天之□。是人也，必命之心以涵天下之□，之身以負天下之極，命之耳目口以□言天下之極。人必盡極，然後可□俯仰無怍。然則天之命我者，大邪小邪？然所以命我者，又必有以託於我也。天不□清，地不能自寧，人物不能自安，必俟夫能盡此極者，付以參贊之責。然則天之託我者，小邪大邪？斯命也，斯託也，惟聖人
translation_en:
…learning. As for [?] establishing a distinctive school of writing in hopes of winning literary renown, or exhaustively annotating the commentary on a single Classic in hopes of joining the ranks of the eminent: these two kinds of scholars are certainly unlike [?] those whose learning narrowly pursues profit and official emoluments. Yet those who eagerly pursue fame are likewise eagerly pursuing advantage. Is this [?] what Heaven has charged me with and entrusted to me? If Heaven’s charge and trust indeed do not lie here, how could the gentleman’s [?] stop here? What, then, is the gentleman’s learning [?]?

That which takes form above is Heaven; that which takes form below is Earth; that which receives its mandate between [?] them is humanity. The Three Powers stand like the three legs of a tripod. Among them are benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue [?], and the apparatus of cultural institutions, rites, and music. This is called Heaven’s [?]. That whereby Heaven is clear, Earth attains tranquility, and humanity attains peace is [?] Heaven’s [?]. To human beings it must grant a heart to contain the world’s [?], a body to bear the world’s ultimate standard, and ears, eyes, and a mouth to [?] express that standard. Only after fully realizing this ultimate standard can a person [?] look down and up without shame. Is Heaven’s charge to me, then, great or small?

Yet in charging me, Heaven must also have something to entrust to me. Heaven cannot [?] be clear; Earth cannot make itself tranquil; human beings and other creatures cannot secure their own peace. It must await someone capable of fully realizing this ultimate standard and confer on that person the responsibility of participating in and assisting the transforming work of Heaven and Earth. Is what Heaven entrusts to me, then, small or great? This charge, this trust—only the sage…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
能盡之達推參贊之功於時窮守參贊之
具於己自聖賢而下未有不須學而能造
入者聖人懼夫後之人生不知學學而
不知所謂大也筆之書以詔後之學者使
□知所依歸下學君子誠知聖人之所教
□天之所以命我託我者率此則公
私□率此則正入彼則邪正且公爲
□成私□邪爲小用如此則進於聖賢如
彼□□於□近□此而窮餓不悔如彼而
===
利□□爲學門戶在大學自格致誠
□而進□以求至乎治平之大知學之精
□□庸必自戒懼愼獨而精之以求至
□□一□學之會論以求存養夫本體
□之七篇以求擴充夫善端學之六經以
求陰□造化之變聖王經理之法析其精
□理於萬事括其大歛萬物於一原優
而游之漸而進之月計不足歲計有餘不
以旦□之益爲功不以尺寸之補爲賢積
punctuated: 能盡之。達，推參贊之功於時；窮，守參贊之具於己。自聖賢而下，未有不須學而能造入者。聖人懼夫後之人生不知學，學而不知所謂大也，筆之書以詔後之學者，使□知所依歸。下學君子誠知聖人之所教，□天之所以命我託我者，率此則公，私□；率此則正，入彼則邪。正且公爲□成，私□邪爲小用。如此則進於聖賢，如彼□□於□近□。此而窮餓不悔，如彼而利□□。爲學門戶在大學，自格致誠□而進□，以求至乎治平之大。知學之精□□庸，必自戒懼愼獨而精之，以求至□□一□。學之會論，以求存養夫本體；□之七篇，以求擴充夫善端；學之六經，以求陰□造化之變、聖王經理之法。析其精□理於萬事，括其大歛萬物於一原。優而游之，漸而進之，月計不足，歲計有餘。不以旦□之益爲功，不以尺寸之補爲賢。積
translation_en:
…can fully realize them. When successful in public life, they extend to their age the work of assisting Heaven and Earth in their transforming and nurturing activity; when in straitened circumstances, they preserve within themselves the resources for that work. From sages and worthies downward, none can attain this without learning. The sages feared that people born in later generations would not know to learn, or would learn without knowing what is meant by greatness. They therefore committed it to writing to instruct later learners, so that [illegible] might know where to turn for guidance. If gentlemen engaged in elementary learning truly understand what the sages teach, [illegible] why Heaven has charged me with this and entrusted this to me [?], then following this leads to impartiality; selfishness [text unclear]. Following this leads to uprightness; entering that other path leads to perversity. Uprightness joined with impartiality makes for [illegible] accomplishment; selfishness [illegible] perversity makes for petty usefulness [?]. Proceeding thus, one advances toward the sages and worthies; proceeding otherwise, [text unclear]. On this path, one feels no regret even in destitution and hunger; on the other, one gains advantage [text unclear].

Beginning with the investigation of things, the extension of knowledge, and making [one’s intentions] sincere [text unclear], one advances in pursuit of the great achievement of governing the state and bringing peace to the world. title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
久而亢然有得所謂天下之極者會之一
心無不足任之一身若有餘入耳無逆經
則天
無障出乎口者足以宣其鬱而達其平
方來嘆□遭抱吾學以自守幸而託身廊
□學以上致吾君下澤吾民納一世
□極□中天工未完我其補之地極未
□我其維之人道未中我其建之日月星
辰□□上□川□不□華於下華夏蠻狄安
===
於□□所□彌綸參贊之責皆於我乎攸
□則天□託於我者至是始無負矣於孰
□吾學爲之也仰觀圓蓋浩無際也俯
□□無涯也吾以了然之身率其所
□至與天地參而兩之可不謂之大成邪
彼覩□利祿者無足與也獨惜夫皓首鑽
□日多而道日晦日視此何如邪抑斯
言也□五峯之言也子思子之言也子思
孟子□後率其大者誰歟河汾二子遭貞
punctuated: 久而亢然有得，所謂天下之極者，會之一心，無不足；任之一身，若有餘。入耳無逆，經則天無障，出乎口者足以宣其鬱而達其平。方來嘆□遭，抱吾學以自守；幸而託身廊□，學以上致吾君，下澤吾民，納一世□極□中。天工未完，我其補之；地極未□，我其維之；人道未中，我其建之。日月星辰□□上，□川□不□華於下，華夏蠻狄安於□□所□。彌綸參贊之責，皆於我乎攸□，則天□託於我者，至是始無負矣。於孰□？吾學爲之也。仰觀圓蓋，浩無際也；俯□□無涯也。吾以了然之身，率其所□，至與天地參而兩之，可不謂之大成邪？彼覩□利祿者，無足與也。獨惜夫皓首鑽□，日多而道日晦，日視此何如邪？抑斯言也，□五峯之言也，子思子之言也。子思、孟子□後，率其大者誰歟？河汾二子遭貞
translation_en:
…After long accumulation, one stands elevated, having gained understanding. What is called the supreme standard of all under Heaven is gathered within a single mind, with nothing lacking; borne by a single person, it seems well within his capacity. What enters the ear meets no resistance; in ordering affairs and taking Heaven as a model, there is no obstruction [?]. What issues from the mouth suffices to express what has been pent up and convey its balance. Lamenting what lies ahead and one's circumstances [?], one holds fast to one's learning to preserve oneself. If fortunate enough to find a place at court [?], one uses learning above to bring one's ruler to fulfillment and below to bestow benefits upon the people, bringing the whole age within the supreme standard and the mean [?]. Where Heaven's work is unfinished, I shall complete it; where Earth's foundations remain […] [?], I shall uphold them; where the human Way has not attained the mean, I shall establish it. The sun, moon, and stars […] above; […] rivers […] flourish below [?]; the peoples of Huaxia and the Man and Di dwell in peace in […] their places [?]. The responsibility for encompassing and ordering all things and assisting the transforming powers of Heaven and Earth rests entirely upon me [?]. Only then will I have fulfilled what Heaven has entrusted to me [?]. Through whose agency is this accomplished [?]? It is my learning that accomplishes it.
Looking up at the rounded canopy of Heaven, I see its vastness without limit; looking down, […] without bounds. With my own lucidly aware person, following what […] until I stand alongside Heaven and Earth and match their powers [?]—can this not be called great fulfillment? Those who look to […] profit and official emoluments are not worthy of participating in this. One can only regret those who, white-haired, continue poring over […] ever more each day, while the Way grows daily more obscure. How does this compare with what has just been described [?]? Yet these words […] are the words of Wufeng, the words of Master Zisi. After Zisi and Mengzi […] who carried forward what was great in their learning? The two masters of He and Fen encountered the Zhen…
