If complete attainment in learning […] rests here, one may perhaps avoid error in one's learning and methods.

□一遠其言荒其簡編脫漏而不可
punctuated:
功爲尤大。甚矣！六經之書皆天地□□寓也。天地能示人以知，而不能人以□；能示人以行，而不能使人必行。必生聖人，聖人以作六經，垂示萬世。天地之望□聖人也厚矣，聖人之補於天地也大矣。其道而燔滅之，不有漢之諸儒□，詎六經之書幾乎泯滅？漢儒不明□鑿之，不有宋之諸儒出而□救，理幾乎□。是漢儒固有功於聖之諸儒□功於聖人也歟？

請因□□陳之。書契之作既成，典籍之興□□。神農黄帝之時，則有三墳，言大；顓頊高辛堯舜之際，則有五典，□道也。八卦之說謂之八索，求其義也；九州之志謂之九丘，叙其聚也。以至攝提□□脩飛流訖等，載簡袠重大，而出□□籍浩繁，而入則充棟。其書不可□一，遠其言荒，其簡編脫漏而不可……
translation_en:
…their contribution was especially great. How momentous! The books of the Six Classics are all repositories of Heaven and Earth’s … [?]. Heaven and Earth can show people how to know, but cannot … [?]; they can show people how to act, but cannot ensure that people will act. Thus sages must be born, and the sages compose the Six Classics to transmit instruction to ten thousand generations. Great indeed are Heaven and Earth’s expectations of the sages [?], and great indeed is what the sages supply to Heaven and Earth. …their Way, and burned and destroyed them [?]. Had there not been the Confucian scholars of the Han …, would the books of the Six Classics not have almost vanished? The Han scholars did not understand … and subjected them to strained interpretations [?]. Had the Confucian scholars of the Song not come forward to … rescue them, their principles would almost have … [?]. Thus the Han scholars certainly rendered service to the sages … did those scholars … render service to the sages? [?]

Allow me, on the basis of …, to set this forth. Once writing had been devised, canonical writings arose … . In the time of Shennong and Huangdi there were the Three Records (San Fen), which spoke of greatness; in the time of Zhuanxu, Gaoxin, Yao, and Shun there were the Five Canons (Wu Dian), … the Way [?]. Explanations of the Eight Trigrams were called the Eight Inquiries (Ba Suo), for they sought out their meaning. Accounts of the Nine Provinces were called the Nine Mounds (Jiu Qiu), for they described what was gathered in them. There were also Sheti … xiu, fei, liu, qi, and others [?]. Recorded on writing slips, their volumes were weighty; when taken out … [?]. The writings were so numerous that, brought indoors, they filled the building. These books could not … one [?]; … distant, their language fantastic [?], their bundles of writing slips incomplete, and they could not …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□矣故吾夫子生獨取詩書禮樂
□□□而刪定之而贊脩之以爲六經
乾□□地造化之文實切於民生日用
之常□地之間不可一日而無也不幸始
□□詩書以愚黔首乃令天下之守尉
時易以卜筮春秋以紀事首末
下逮秦火詩雖相傳亡其六篇或謂
□原未有詞是詩亦未嘗亡也禮
門□□□無成書且純駁相半
===
亦未□□之疵也所可恨者獨
周之書百篇缺亡殆盡有漢肇興
□旁求儒雅以闡大猷濟南伏生
失其本經口傳二十餘篇魯共
□壞□子宅爲宮又於壁間得所藏書
增多□生二十五篇餘皆不可得已或曰
□□之國尚有存者特以禁嚴不入
□未可知已當是之時易與尚書
□何以有傳焉詩與禮樂賴申公
punctuated: □矣。故吾夫子生，獨取詩書禮樂□□□而刪定之，而贊脩之，以爲六經。乾□□地造化之文，實切於民生日用之常，□地之間不可一日而無也。不幸始□□詩書以愚黔首，乃令天下之守尉，時易以卜筮，春秋以紀事首末。下逮秦火，詩雖相傳，亡其六篇。或謂□原未有詞，是詩亦未嘗亡也。禮門□□□無成書，且純駁相半，亦未□□之疵也。所可恨者，獨周之書百篇缺亡殆盡。有漢肇興，□旁求儒雅以闡大猷。濟南伏生失其本經，口傳二十餘篇。魯共□壞□子宅爲宮，又於壁間得所藏書，增多□生二十五篇，餘皆不可得已。或曰：□□之國尚有存者，特以禁嚴不入，□未可知已。當是之時，易與尚書□何以有傳焉？詩與禮樂賴申公
translation_en:
…[illegible]. Thus, when our Master was born, he selected only the Poetry, Documents, Rites, Music, and [illegible], abridging and establishing their texts, and contributing to their revision, to make the Six Classics. Their writings concerning the creative transformations of Heaven and Earth [?] bear directly upon the ordinary needs of the people's daily lives; within Heaven and Earth [?], they cannot be dispensed with for even a single day. Unfortunately, [the First Emperor?] [illegible] the Poetry and Documents to keep the common people ignorant, and then ordered the defenders and commandants throughout the realm [unclear]. The Changes served for divination, and the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded events from beginning to end [?]. By the time of the Qin book burning, although the Poetry continued to be transmitted, six of its pieces had been lost. Some say that [illegible] originally had no words, so that these poems had never actually been lost. As for the Rites, [illegible] there was no complete book, and authentic and mixed material each accounted for half; yet [the assessment of its defects is unclear]. What alone merits lament is that the hundred chapters of the Zhou Documents were almost entirely lost.

When the Han dynasty first arose, [illegible] sought learned scholars far and wide to elucidate the grand Way. Fu Sheng of Jinan had lost his original text of the classic and transmitted more than twenty chapters orally. King Gong of Lu [?] demolished the Master's residence [?] to build a palace, and writings stored within its walls were discovered. These added twenty-five chapters to those of Fu Sheng [?]; none of the remainder could be recovered. Some say that copies still survived in the state of [illegible], but that stringent prohibitions alone prevented their entry; [illegible] this remained uncertain. At that time, how was it that the Changes and the Book of Documents [illegible] were transmitted? The Poetry, Rites, and Music depended upon Shen Gong …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
以有傳馬春秋賴公羊穀梁鄒氏
□傳馬之數儒皆有功於聖經者
□□家之徒散布甚衆人持一經而
□□開□牖人挾一見而各騁軌轍此所以
經□壞於秦火而壞於漢儒之議也
九江鳳鳴周程張朱相繼而出
□續孔孟千載不傳之緒得有所
□二家似是之非程子作易傳朱
我□沉□傳而易旨之理燦然
□□詩□安國作春秋傳陳澔
□說而詩春秋禮樂之理昭然益
□穿鑿不破而自息孔孟之正宗
===
□柰何文王周公之易本卜筮
也程子易傳專以理言所以論君子
□變□發自暴自棄之說論君子得與而
□風泉之論其與文周之易若相背
□□曰不看本文自成一書非以此
□春秋魯之史記也而胡氏春秋
punctuated:
以有傳馬？春秋賴公羊、穀梁、鄒氏□傳馬？之數儒，皆有功於聖經者。□□家之徒，散布甚衆，人持一經而□□開□牖，人挾一見而各騁軌轍。此所以經□壞於秦火，而壞於漢儒之議也。
九江鳳鳴，周、程、張、朱相繼而出，□續孔孟千載不傳之緒，得有所□。二家似是之非，程子作《易傳》，朱我□沉□傳，而易旨之理燦然。□□詩□安國作《春秋傳》，陳澔□說，而詩、春秋、禮樂之理昭然益□，穿鑿不破而自息，孔孟之正宗□。
柰何文王、周公之易，本卜筮也，程子《易傳》專以理言，所以論君子□變□發自暴自棄之說，論君子得與而□風泉之論，其與文、周之易若相背。□□曰：「不看本文，自成一書。」非以此□？春秋，魯之史記也，而胡氏春秋
translation_en:
…thereby continued to be transmitted [?]. Did the Spring and Autumn Annals likewise depend upon Gongyang, Guliang, and Zou for their transmission [?]? These several scholars all rendered service to the canonical writings of the sages. The adherents of the [illegible] schools were very widely dispersed. Each upheld a single classic and opened [his own] window of interpretation [?]; each clung to a single view and pursued his own course. This is why the classics [illegible] were ruined by the Qin fires, yet were also ruined by the arguments of Han scholars.
At Jiujiang the phoenix cried [?], and Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu emerged in succession. They carried on the thread of Confucius and Mencius, which had gone untransmitted for a thousand years, and found something upon which to [illegible]. Against the plausible errors of the two schools [?], Master Cheng composed his Commentary on the Changes; Zhu [the wording concerning his commentary is corrupt], and the principles underlying the Changes shone brilliantly. [Corrupt text concerning the Odes] Anguo composed a Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Chen Hao [expounded his] explanations [?]. Thus the principles of the Odes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, rites, and music became increasingly clear [illegible]. Forced interpretations subsided of themselves without needing refutation, and the orthodox lineage of Confucius and Mencius [illegible].
Yet how is it that the Changes of King Wen and the Duke of Zhou was originally concerned with divination, whereas Master Cheng’s Commentary on the Changes speaks exclusively in terms of principle? Thus, in discussing the gentleman’s [illegible] changes [?], he develops an account of doing violence to oneself and abandoning oneself; in discussing the gentleman’s gaining associates [?], he offers a discussion of wind and springs [?]. His work seems at odds with the Changes of King Wen and the Duke of Zhou. [Illegible] said: “Without attending to the original text, he makes a separate book of his own.” Was this not the reason [?]? The Spring and Autumn Annals was the historical record of Lu, yet Master Hu’s [commentary on the] Spring and Autumn Annals…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□明事或求一字以爲一事之是非
□以爲一人之得失其與孔子之
意□之矣故晦菴曰多牽强處不合聖
□忠非此歟夫六經之道未嘗不同六經
□未嘗不異善學者德益進而業益脩
□温柔敦厚易書詩之教也務易
之務書而趨於事務詩而溺其志
□流日遠而弊日甚如潔淨精微
無□誣自民之愚其能免
===
恭□敬莊儉傳多良春秋禮
□屬比而作其法禮亡其體樂徇
□之亂過當之煩好大之奢其能
□善學者之所致爾若善學者
□深卷之固見天地之純全古人之大
體亦無此失矣豈謂載道之經明道之
□於此哉雖然天位乎上使無日
□以成乎天地位乎下使無山川
成乎地上天下地之字往古來
punctuated:
□明事，或求一字以爲一事之是非，□以爲一人之得失，其與孔子之意□之矣。故晦菴曰：「多牽强處，不合聖□忠。」非此歟？夫六經之道未嘗不同，六經□未嘗不異。善學者德益進而業益脩。□温柔敦厚，易、書、詩之教也。務易之務書而趨於事，務詩而溺其志，□流日遠而弊日甚。如潔淨精微，無□誣，自民之愚，其能免？

恭□敬莊儉，傳多良，春秋、禮□屬比而作其法，禮亡其體，樂徇□之亂、過當之煩、好大之奢，其能□？善學者之所致爾。若善學者，□深卷之固，見天地之純全、古人之大體，亦無此失矣。豈謂載道之經、明道之□於此哉？雖然，天位乎上，使無日□，以成乎天地位乎下，使無山川成乎地。上天下地之字，往古來
translation_en:
…[?] elucidate affairs; sometimes they seek in a single character a judgment of the right or wrong of an affair, [?] taking it to indicate a person's success or failure. Their relation to Confucius's intention is [?]. Thus Hui'an said: “There are many strained interpretations that do not accord with the sage's [?].” Was this not what he meant? The Way of the Six Classics has never been other than one, yet the Six Classics [?] have never been without differences. Those who learn well advance further in virtue and become more accomplished in their undertakings. [?] Gentleness, kindness, sincerity, and generosity are teachings of the Book of Changes, the Book of Documents, and the Book of Odes [?]. Concentrating on the Changes [?]; concentrating on the Documents, one becomes engrossed in affairs; concentrating on the Odes, one lets one's aspirations become submerged. [?] The current strays farther each day, and the harmful consequences grow worse. As for purity and subtle precision, without [?] falsehood, and the people's ignorance [?]—can these be avoided?

Reverence [?], respect, solemnity, and frugality; transmitting much goodness [?]. The Spring and Autumn Annals and the Rites [?]: arranging and comparing events to establish their rules [?]; ritual loses its essential form, and music follows [?]. Can the resulting disorder, the vexations of excess, and the extravagance of grand ambitions [?] be avoided? These are brought about by those who learn well [?]. As for those who learn well, [?] depth and firmness [the transcription is unclear], they perceive the purity and wholeness of Heaven and Earth and the broad principles of the ancients, and thus avoid these failings. How could one say that the classics that bear the Way and the [?] that elucidate the Way [come to] this [?]? Nevertheless, Heaven occupies the position above: if it lacked the sun [?], [how could it] constitute Heaven [?]? Earth occupies the position below: if it lacked mountains and rivers, [how could it] constitute Earth [?]? Heaven above and Earth below [the following character is doubtful]; antiquity past and time to come …

□是六經雖作於聖人而實關乎
天地□經者天地之道也聖人既生道在
聖人既往道在六經天豈能忘情於
此觀之秦火一然漢儒競出穿
□儒迭興天地未必無深意於其

translation_en:
…If the Six Classics did not circulate between them, there would likewise be no means of completing □ [?]. Heaven does not withhold the Way, and earth does not withhold its treasures; thus sages are bountifully born. □ Although these Six Classics were composed by sages, they are indeed bound up with Heaven and Earth. The □ Classics embody the Way of Heaven and Earth. When the sages were alive, the Way was present; once the sages had passed away, the Way resided in the Six Classics. How could Heaven be indifferent to this? Consider how, once the fires of Qin had blazed, Han scholars emerged in competition, and scholars arose in succession [穿□儒, doubtful]. Heaven and Earth may well have had a profound intention in this…

Liu Qidong

〔“This is a case that has remained unsettled for □ several years [?]. This policy essay passes judgment on antiquity, like Zigong setting out the advantages and disadvantages between two armies.”〕〔“The envoy has not yet returned [?]; in discussing affairs of government, his righteous spirit overwhelms the reader. Having obtained a candidate like this, the presiding examiner need not blush with shame.”〕

□ There are things one wishes to extend to later ages that may nevertheless prove impracticable; the partiality of laws □ in later ages may nevertheless be incapable [of implementation?]. title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
最私也後所有而古人之所無也
□有不能如鹽鐵之法可以行於後
□有不能如封建之法可以廢於今
□昔相不逮秦漢任法之主秦漢君
□虞周作法之聖哉愚嘗展轉思之
公則天私則人公則人私則已
□已兼并之念私則便已取給之情
□過亦勢所遭而然也夫豈道之
□諸侯분天下之田與
===
□國與有以者同自秦
□後世相沿雖賢如唐太宗輔以
□古今事殊竟不克復當代儒臣
□恩見未一柳宗元建論以爲封
□聖之意也勢也極推先代相承之敝
□邑之宜不必拘泥古制宋范蘇二
□□之獨致堂胡寅爲之說曰封建
□世所以順天理承天心公天下之大
□也郡縣者覇世暴主所以縱人欲
punctuated: 最私也，後所有而古人之所無也。□有不能如鹽鐵之法，可以行於後；□有不能如封建之法，可以廢於今。□昔相不逮，秦漢任法之主，秦漢君□虞周作法之聖哉？愚嘗展轉思之：公則天，私則人；公則人，私則已。□已兼并之念，私則便已取給之情。□過亦勢所遭而然也，夫豈道之□？諸侯분天下之田，與□國與有以者同。自秦□後世相沿，雖賢如唐太宗，輔以□，古今事殊，竟不克復。當代儒臣□恩見未一，柳宗元建論，以爲封□聖之意也，勢也，極推先代相承之敝，□邑之宜，不必拘泥古制。宋范蘇二□□之，獨致堂胡寅爲之說曰：「封建□世所以順天理、承天心、公天下之大□也；郡縣者，覇世暴主所以縱人欲……
translation_en: …is the most self-serving; it is something that existed in later times but did not exist among the ancients. □ Some cannot, like the salt and iron system, be implemented in later ages; □ some cannot, like the system of enfeoffment, be abolished in the present. □ Past and present fall short of one another [?]. The rulers of Qin and Han relied upon laws; were the sovereigns of Qin and Han □ the sages of Yu and Zhou who established laws [?]? I have repeatedly pondered this: what is public accords with Heaven; what is private accords with human desires. What is public serves others; what is private serves oneself. □ thoughts of annexation for oneself [?]; what is private expresses the desire to benefit oneself and obtain supplies. □ Faults, too, arise from the circumstances encountered; how could this be □ of the Way? The regional lords [divided?] the lands of the realm; □ states and those possessing the means were alike [?]. From Qin □, subsequent ages followed the same practice. Even a ruler as worthy as Tang Taizong, assisted by □, ultimately could not restore the former system, because circumstances differed between antiquity and the present. The Confucian officials of the time □ did not agree in their views [?]. Liu Zongyuan advanced an argument that enfeoffment □ was a matter of circumstances, rather than the sages’ intention [?]. He thoroughly expounded the accumulated abuses inherited from earlier ages and the suitability of □ settlements, maintaining that there was no need to adhere rigidly to ancient institutions. The two Song writers Fan and Su □□ it [?]. Hu Yin, known as Zhitang, alone offered this explanation: “Enfeoffment □ is the great □ through which an age follows Heaven’s principles, receives Heaven’s intentions, and makes the realm public to all. Commanderies and counties are the means by which violent rulers in an age of hegemony indulge human desires …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□□一身之大孽大賊也論辯千言如
□□判獄聽者頷首此不易之言也然
□既時更勢積譬之黃河南決奔流倒

===

punctuated: □嫌隙，如契丹歲幣之數，獻與之□也。然心如車人之推轂，轂行則爲同轂。殳遺母，考叔之孝也；莊而還母，則其孝又有以忠其君矣。□千房之節也，沛公破秦而竟從□，又足以保身矣。鄧禹追見光□，一見語合而成平與之業。岳天復唾手燕雲，大功垂成而竟沮□，當高宗一世，非光武□成。温公之相元祐，力不旋乾轉□之功；武侯之遇昭烈，□而不能成誅操破孫之績。盖孔□衰，非宋祚之隆盛，功烏乎其□？顧以道學倡天下。孫何、孫僅也，一時同一兄弟也。然文章惟魁，學則傳於萬世，文章豈道學匹？□著忠勲於光武，夷簡、公著膺□哲，同一父子也。然夷簡相才雖

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□則不足夷簡豈賈復儔乎之數
□之產非天下之賢聖則一時
何容喙哉然有一說焉伊尹樊
□言矣自漢而下諸公之勳之德
□未盡則取之或未明則不可也
□獻是故以將畧言之子房謀
□百中佐漢高定一天下皆其
□八陣之圖木牛流馬之法佐昭
□也岳飛以八百衆而
===
□目而淪□於湖湘
□受約束□議棄燕山其茂績又
□相業言韓琦佐仁宗則西戎寒
□佐英廟則捲聽政之簾調兩
□也富弼之河北燕然手所撫
□庭士夫相慶何傑也溫公與呂
□哲宗明道稱爲二龍都人留爲
□豈之宿弊復慶曆之舊觀又何
□道學言之明道如春風育物雖
punctuated: □則不足，夷簡豈賈復儔乎？之數□之產，非天下之賢聖，則一時何容喙哉？然有一說焉：伊尹、樊□言矣。自漢而下，諸公之勳之德，□未盡則取之，或未明則不可也。□獻，是故以將畧言之，子房謀□百中，佐漢高定一天下，皆其□。八陣之圖、木牛流馬之法，佐昭□也。岳飛以八百衆而□目，而淪□於湖湘，□受約束，□議棄燕山，其茂績又□。相業言，韓琦佐仁宗，則西戎寒□；佐英廟，則捲聽政之簾，調兩□也。富弼之河北燕然，手所撫□，庭士夫相慶，何傑也！溫公與呂□哲宗，明道稱爲二龍，都人留爲□，豈之宿弊，復慶曆之舊觀，又何□？道學言之，明道如春風育物，雖
translation_en: …was nevertheless insufficient [?]. How could Yijian compare with Jia Fu? The number of these […] and their emergence [?]—if they were not the worthy and sage men of the realm, then who in their time could presume to criticize them [?]? Yet there is something to be said: Yi Yin and Fan […] have been discussed [?]. As for the achievements and virtues of the various gentlemen from the Han onward, […] if not exhausted, then select them; if not made clear, this will not do [?]. […] Thus, speaking of military strategy, Zifang’s plans […] succeeded a hundred times out of a hundred. His assistance to Gaozu of Han in unifying the realm was all his […]. The diagram of the Eight Formations and the methods of the wooden oxen and flowing horses assisted Zhao[…] [?]. Yue Fei, with eight hundred men, […] and sank […] in the Hunan region; […] submitted to orders, […] proposed abandoning Yanshan. His outstanding achievements, moreover, […]. Speaking of achievements as chief councilor, when Han Qi assisted Emperor Renzong, the western Rong trembled […]; when he assisted Emperor Yingzong, he rolled up the curtain from behind which government affairs were heard and reconciled the two […] sides [?]. Fu Bi’s […] in Hebei, peaceful and settled [?], were personally soothed by him […]; the gentlemen of the court congratulated one another. How outstanding he was! Duke Wen and Lü […] Emperor Zhezong; Mingdao […] were called the Two Dragons [?], and the people of the capital detained them as […] [?]. […] longstanding abuses and restored the former splendor of the Qingli era—how […]! Speaking of the Learning of the Way, Mingdao was like a spring breeze nurturing all things, although…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□惡伊川欲坐而講道雖黨議不
之錄輝於星斗正義之編昭如
立德立言而功垂於萬世者也
□以功名終貫復以剛直著亦賢
□者上攀伊尹仲山甫之駕次
□則追子房韓富諸公之蹤苟
□當傳二程之脉絡如此則下可
□立命上可以爲國家開太平我
□下以我爲賢哉管見
===
也
□趙繼英
□訓導汪　批　大凡圖事揆策必胸中卓
□後措諸言論如懸河倒海論黃河於今日不當如是耶昔
□不求辦事之人而求曉事之人子論河於昔日叙論河於今日如此可謂
者矣技于以進欲覽觀者溟之浩瀚也
□訓導逯　批　古人不出門而知天下之事此策論
□河遷省灼有定見雖陳賈復生無以易此蓋若子者可與論事矣
punctuated:
□惡，伊川欲坐而講道，雖黨議不之錄，輝於星斗；正義之編，昭如。立德立言，而功垂於萬世者也。□以功名終，貫復以剛直著，亦賢□者。上攀伊尹、仲山甫之駕，次□則追子房、韓、富諸公之蹤。苟□當傳二程之脉絡，如此則下可□立命，上可以爲國家開太平。我□下以我爲賢哉？管見也。
□趙繼英。
□訓導汪　批：大凡圖事揆策，必胸中卓□，後措諸言論，如懸河倒海。論黃河於今日，不當如是耶？昔□不求辦事之人，而求曉事之人。子論河於昔日叙，論河於今日如此，可謂者矣。技于以進，欲覽觀者溟之浩瀚也。
□訓導逯　批：古人不出門而知天下之事。此策論□河遷省，灼有定見。雖陳、賈復生，無以易此。蓋若子者，可與論事矣。
translation_en:
…[illegible] evil [?]. Yichuan wished to sit and expound the Way. Although partisan criticism did not [the wording is defective here], the record shone among the stars; the compilation of correct interpretations was as bright as … [?]. These were men who established virtue and enduring teachings, whose achievements would benefit ten thousand generations. [Illegible] ended his life with merit and renown; Guan [?], in turn, became known for uprightness and integrity, and was also a worthy [illegible]. At the highest level, one should aspire to follow Yi Yin and Zhong Shanfu; next, [illegible], one should follow in the footsteps of Zifang and such men as Han and Fu. If [illegible], one ought to transmit the intellectual lineage of the two Cheng brothers. In this way, at the lower level one could [illegible] establish one’s allotted destiny, and at the higher level inaugurate an age of great peace for the state. Would our [illegible] regard me as worthy [?]? Such is my limited view.
[Illegible] Zhao Jiying.
[Illegible] Assistant Instructor Wang’s comment: In general, when planning undertakings and weighing strategies, one must first have something firmly established [illegible] in one’s mind; only then should one express it in words, like a river pouring down or a sea cascading forth. Should discussion of the Yellow River today not be like this? Formerly, [illegible] sought people who understood affairs rather than people who merely carried them out. Your account of the river in earlier times and your discussion of it today are like this: you may indeed be called such a person [?]. Your skill thereby advances; what one wishes to behold is the ocean’s vastness [?].
[Illegible] Assistant Instructor Lu’s comment: The ancients knew the affairs of the world without leaving their doors. This policy essay discusses [illegible] the river and moving the provincial administration [?], displaying clear and settled judgments. Even if Chen and Jia returned to life, they could not improve upon it. Someone like you is indeed a person with whom affairs can be discussed.

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□試官訓導朱　批〔治河一策正欲試士子平居□□之志此篇處置得宜一如子言則河爲安流而城爲定阯漕汴〕
〔□□之可以銳挽矣〕
□學正秦　批〔此策自胸中流出非卓有定見〕
〔□□□於子平居講之素矣〕
教授李　批〔知古蹟識時務如身臨而足及者〕
〔□空言者比耶〕
可也慮其不北今之治河也慮其
民害爲□重今之治河
===
□治河也乚夫天下之水黃河爲
□患黃河爲大執事策河南之士
入者愚也飲河水而但知有飽
□問乎然聞諸故老嘗有得於
□自神禹以來世變時更遷徙無
而下地平土疏衝决無常漢世
入勢雖北亦嘗有時而南徙矣
迹尚存一失而漫流無紀自元迄
今之勢□達變通之宜
punctuated:
□試官訓導朱批〔治河一策，正欲試士子平居□□之志。此篇處置得宜，一如子言，則河爲安流，而城爲定阯，漕汴〕〔□□之可以銳挽矣。〕
□學正秦批〔此策自胸中流出，非卓有定見〕〔□□□於子平居講之素矣。〕
教授李批〔知古蹟，識時務，如身臨而足及者〕〔□空言者比耶？〕
可也，慮其不北。今之治河也，慮其民害爲□重。今之治河，□治河也，乚夫天下之水，黃河爲□患，黃河爲大。執事策河南之士，入者愚也，飲河水而但知有飽□問乎？然聞諸故老，嘗有得於□。自神禹以來，世變時更，遷徙無，而下地平土疏，衝决無常。漢世入勢雖北，亦嘗有時而南徙矣。迹尚存，一失而漫流無紀。自元迄今之勢，□達變通之宜。
translation_en:
Examiner [?] Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “This policy question on controlling the river is intended precisely to test the aspirations that candidates ordinarily hold concerning [two illegible characters]. This essay proposes appropriate measures. If everything were done as you suggest, the river would flow peacefully and the city would stand on firm foundations. Grain transport on the Bian [?] … could be vigorously drawn along [?].”
Qin, a Director of Studies [preceding character illegible], comments: “This policy essay flows from your own mind. Without firmly established views … [three illegible characters] … the sustained study you have ordinarily devoted to this.”
Li, a Prefectural School Professor, comments: “You know the traces of the past and understand present affairs, as though you had personally visited these places and walked over the ground. … Could someone who offers empty words compare with you?”
“… would be acceptable; the concern is that it will not flow north. In controlling the river today, the concern is that the harm to the people is [illegible character] severe. In controlling the river today … controlling the river … [garbled text]. Of all the waters under Heaven, the Yellow River constitutes … a calamity; the Yellow River is the greatest. You, sir, have posed a policy question to the scholars of Henan. The one who enters [?] is my foolish self: drinking the river’s water, I know only that I have had my fill … ask? Yet I have heard accounts from the elders and have gained some understanding from … . Since the time of the divine Yu, generations and circumstances have changed, and its course has shifted without … . Downstream, the land is level and the soil loose; breaches occur unpredictably. In Han times, although its course tended northward [?], it also sometimes shifted south. Traces still remain. Once control was lost, it spread unchecked. From the Yuan down to the present, its configuration … the appropriate ways to adapt to changing circumstances …”

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□勢雖南時以遷道居東一決而
□故司河渠者一挽狂瀾而北倒
而南之其勢使然也執事北而
今運河要害無如安平鎮而河
□此鎮之門户也此門不塞則
守黄陵岡失守則安平鎮可慮
□矣今運河險峻無如徐呂二洪
□家道口則二洪之咽喉也此口
□□同不□則二洪淺澁
===
□□使者□則塞其害之
□其利之不夫道一而已矣執事
□非矣漢賈讓欲內徙民居以爲
大河以入渤海將建千載之業
□之地策寔上矣然施於漢世可
□東郡適漕運之途清河乃舟楫
□讓策於今日則運道所經或高
隄岸或深之而爲黄流今則𤅢矣
punctuated:
□勢雖南，時以遷道居東，一決而□。故司河渠者，一挽狂瀾而北倒，而南之，其勢使然也。執事北而今運河要害，無如安平鎮，而河□此鎮之門户也。此門不塞，則守黄陵岡；失守，則安平鎮可慮□矣。今運河險峻，無如徐呂二洪，□家道口則二洪之咽喉也。此口□□同不□，則二洪淺澁。
□□使者□，則塞其害之□，其利之不，夫道一而已矣。執事□非矣。漢賈讓欲內徙民居，以爲大河，以入渤海，將建千載之業，□之地，策寔上矣。然施於漢世可，□東郡適漕運之途，清河乃舟楫□。讓策於今日，則運道所經，或高隄岸，或深之而爲黄流，今則𤅢矣。
translation_en:
…Although its course tends southward [?], at times it shifts its channel eastward; once it breaches the embankment, [illegible]. Thus those administering the rivers and canals seek to turn the raging waters back northward, yet direct them southward [?]: the configuration of the river compels this. You, honored examiners, [fragment concerning the north, unclear]. At present, no strategic point on the Grand Canal is more critical than Anping Zhen, and [an illegible river reference] is the gateway to this town. If this gateway is not blocked, then Huangling Gang must be held; if it is lost, Anping Zhen will be in danger [?]. Among the canal’s perilous stretches, none surpass the two rapids at Xu and Lü. [Illegible]jia Daokou is the throat of these two rapids. If this opening [illegible condition], the two rapids will become shallow and difficult to navigate.
[Illegible passage mentioning a commissioner.] Then block what causes harm [?] and [unclear passage concerning its benefits]; there is but one guiding principle. You, honored examiners, [unclear statement concerning error]. Jia Rang of the Han wished to move the inhabitants inland to make room for the great river to flow into the Bohai Sea, thereby establishing an achievement that would endure for a thousand years. [Unclear reference to land.] His policy was indeed of the highest order. Yet while it could be implemented in Han times, [illegible] Dongjun lies directly on the grain-transport route, and Qinghe is [an illegible statement concerning boats]. If Rang’s policy were applied today, along the course of the transport route one might raise the embankments or deepen the channel to accommodate the Yellow River’s waters; today, however, [the concluding expression is unclear: 𤅢] [?].

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□以古法不能推於今此亦可以驗
□治湖通渠導江舟以達淮引汶
□舟以達衛轉江南之財賦給冀
□則儒矣然施之於今日可也
長安淮之漕舟不入于汴汴之
□河推瑄蹟於先代導淮之功
□汴二洪之業莫施於三門古則
□不能□於古此亦可
===
□來□當慮者金龍
□之門介□之心不可不謹近時
□欲於南流之下分數河以泄上
□深矣愚嘗觀南流最下淮泗
□河口匯而為一惟一道以奔
□以疏河為斯策者蓋亦未試其
流既滯則上流必壅吾懼此口

□來□當慮者金龍□之門，介□之心不可不謹。近時□欲於南流之下分數河，以泄上□，深矣。愚嘗觀南流最下，淮泗□河口匯而為一，惟一道以奔□。以疏河為斯策者，蓋亦未試其流。既滯，則上流必壅。吾懼此口□將為涸轍矣，可終不為計乎？汴□隄之下，復隍之戒不可不思。近時

Yet these measures can be applied today. Chang’an … the grain-transport boats of the Huai did not enter the Bian; the Bian’s … river [?]. title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□議欲擇形勝便地遷省城以避河
□亦至矣愚嘗觀省城之內
□轃鱗居無類萬計當民窮財困
舊營新之舉晝此議者蓋亦不
□然因循數年河日以淤城日以
封一損汴城將爲釜魚矣可終
考古治河之法不出曰疏曰濬
□必三策□舉而後大患可圖今
□而無□害之止兒啼
===
者有隄而無濬譬之防民口而塞
畜而不泄不可得已欲探策於
□無患不可得已今之
流有殺而後金龍口無壅滯之
□濬而後汴城無潰決之危淇

一沽竊謂宜於武陽舊道疏河流
引於淇門北入于海又於館陶
長隄以防東潰則上流勢殺而金
punctuated: □議欲擇形勝便地，遷省城以避河，□亦至矣。愚嘗觀省城之內，□轃鱗居，無類萬計。當民窮財困，舊營新之舉，晝此議者蓋亦不□。然因循數年，河日以淤，城日以封，一損，汴城將爲釜魚矣，可終？考古治河之法，不出曰疏曰濬，□必三策□舉，而後大患可圖。今□而無□，害之止兒啼者，有隄而無濬，譬之防民口而塞，畜而不泄，不可得已。欲探策於□，無患不可得已。今之流有殺，而後金龍口無壅滯之□；濬而後汴城無潰決之危。淇道也，今此水東與衛合，北會清，一沽。竊謂宜於武陽舊道疏河流，引於淇門，北入于海；又於館陶長隄，以防東潰，則上流勢殺而金
translation_en:
…The proposal is to choose conveniently situated, strategically advantageous ground and relocate the provincial capital to escape the river; □, too, has reached its utmost [?]. I have observed within the provincial capital □, dwellings packed like fish scales, numbering in the tens of thousands [?]. With the people impoverished and resources exhausted, the undertaking of [abandoning?] the old and building anew—the person who devised this proposal presumably also did not □ [?]. Yet, after several years of delay, the river silts up daily and the city becomes increasingly hemmed in [?]. Once damage occurs, Biancheng will be like a fish in a cooking pot. Can this go on indefinitely [?]?

Examining ancient methods of river management, one finds nothing beyond opening channels and dredging. □ The three measures must □ be undertaken together before this great menace can be addressed. Now, □ without □—[the passage concerning harm and stopping a child's crying is unclear]. To have embankments without dredging is like stopping up the people's mouths: to impound without releasing cannot be sustained [?]. To seek a strategy in □ and obtain freedom from trouble [the wording is unclear]. Only after the force of the present current has been reduced will Jinlongkou be free from blockage □; only after dredging will Biancheng be free from the danger of breached embankments.

[This is?] the course of the Qi River. Today this water joins the Wei River to the east and meets the Qing River to the north, [then reaches?] Gu [?]. I humbly suggest opening a channel along the old course at Wuyang, diverting the river through Qimen and northward into the sea. Furthermore, [a long embankment should be built?] at Guantao to prevent a breach to the east. Then the force of the upstream current would diminish, and Jin…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□砥柱矣朱仙鎮古蔡河道也今
河通南會潁汝以達正陽竊謂
□舊口濬河流五分之一引於蔡
淮又於祥符以南作長隄以防
□流勢分而汴城安於磐石矣又
之金龍口居河之北汴梁居河
則汴梁無慮南傾則金龍口無
□濬二地□有一害上流兩殺二
□以導□殺一以從南
===
下流泄而□無壅滯左右殺而中
□人岐□之□亳之宿之
道永賴既全大利於天下汴藩
□患於一方此策果建豈曰小
□事至再至三拳拳爲中州慮
慮患於中州者曰黃河也愚竊
患尚有大於黃河者執事未之
而鳴人必以爲悻倘與其進焉
於家者一鳴
punctuated:
□砥柱矣。朱仙鎮，古蔡河道也。今河通，南會潁汝，以達正陽。竊謂□舊口，濬河流五分之一，引於蔡淮；又於祥符以南作長隄，以防□，流勢分而汴城安於磐石矣。又之金龍口居河之北，汴梁居河，則汴梁無慮；南傾則金龍口無□。濬二地，□有一害；上流兩殺，二□以導□，殺一以從南。下流泄而□無壅滯，左右殺而中□。人岐□之□亳之宿之，道永賴。既全大利於天下，汴藩□患於一方。此策果建，豈曰小□？
事至再至三，拳拳爲中州慮。慮患於中州者曰黃河也。愚竊□患尚有大於黃河者，執事未之，而鳴人必以爲悻。倘與其進焉，於家者一鳴。
translation_en:
…[illegible] would stand like a pillar against the current. Zhuxian Zhen lies on the ancient course of the Cai River. The river now connects southward with the Ying and Ru rivers, reaching Zhengyang. I humbly propose [restoring?] the old outlet, dredging a channel for one-fifth of the river’s flow, and directing it into the Cai and Huai rivers. A long dike should also be built south of Xiangfu to guard against [illegible]. The force of the current would thus be divided, and Biancheng would be as secure as a great rock. Furthermore [?], Jinlong Kou lies north of the river, while Bianliang lies [location missing] relative to the river; then Bianliang would have nothing to fear. If the flow inclined southward, Jinlong Kou would be without [illegible]. Dredging at the two places [would leave?] one danger; reducing the force upstream in both directions, two [illegible] would guide [illegible], reducing one to follow southward [?]. The flow downstream would drain away, and [illegible] would suffer no obstruction. Its force would be reduced to left and right, while the middle [illegible]. The passage mentioning people, Qi [?], Bo, and Su is corrupt; the watercourse would provide lasting benefit [?]. This would secure a great benefit for all under Heaven, while the princely domain at Bian would [avert?] danger in its own region. If this proposal were indeed implemented, could it be called a minor [illegible]?
The matter has arisen twice and three times; I remain earnestly concerned for Zhongzhou. Those who consider the dangers facing Zhongzhou name the Yellow River. I humbly [submit?] that there is a danger still greater than the Yellow River. You, sir, have not [recognized it?]; yet if I speak out, others will surely consider me rash and obstinate. If you would permit its presentation [?]—one utterance by someone at home [?]…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□學者之分也亦豈學者之責也
□其狂簡而裁之
punctuated: □學者之分也，亦豈學者之責也？□其狂簡而裁之。
translation_en: …[?] is the scholar’s duty; yet is it the scholar’s responsibility? [?] May you correct his rash and insufficiently considered words.

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□鄉試錄後序
制越三載天下有司
興隸蜀之賢以
二年正德丁卯寔維
也巡按河南監察御史
□□□諸□預聘〔鑑〕
===
□□□□至其合提學
使宋〔禮〕所選士千六百
閩棘三試之得文詞
□□者八十人擇其尤
十篇繕刻成書
□與主司僉謂宜有言
punctuated:
□鄉試錄後序

制越三載，天下有司興隸蜀之賢，以二年正德丁卯，寔維也。巡按河南監察御史□□□諸□預聘〔鑑〕，□□□□至其合提學使宋〔禮〕所選士千六百，閩棘三試之，得文詞□□者八十人。擇其尤十篇，繕刻成書。□與主司僉謂宜有言。
translation_en:
□ Afterword to the Provincial Examination Record

By regulation, every three years the responsible authorities throughout the realm … recommended worthy men belonging to Shu [?]. In the second year of Zhengde, the dingmao year [1507] … [the connecting text is garbled]. The Regional Inspector of Henan, an Investigating Censor, □□□諸□, engaged in advance 〔Jian〕 [?]. □□□□ … together with the 1,600 candidates selected by Education Intendant Song 〔Li〕, they were examined in three sessions within the examination compound [?]. Eighty men whose compositions were □□ were obtained. Ten particularly outstanding essays were selected, copied out, and engraved for printing as a book. □ and the presiding examination officials all agreed that some words should be written.

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□簡竊惟河南迺中州
區分七郡以總其綱
而分屬之州縣百有
□百一十有五間之
□舜而談道德之士不
萬餘加以吏民之秀辟
尺箸弟子之
===
□□□□吐氣思策一
於有道之世僥首就試
學止拔千六百有奇
試焉纔得十之一已
五房分較一經主司
覈之再披再閱胥審
□詞嚴誼正質聖賢經
punctuated: □簡，竊惟河南迺中州，區分七郡以總其綱，而分屬之州縣百有□百一十有五。間之□舜，而談道德之士不萬餘，加以吏民之秀，辟尺箸弟子之□□□□，吐氣思策一於有道之世，僥首就試。學止拔千六百有奇，試焉纔得十之一已。五房分較一經，主司覈之，再披再閱，胥審□詞嚴誼正，質聖賢經
translation_en: …[inscribed on] slips [?]. I humbly consider that Henan is the Central Region. It is divided into seven prefectures to provide its overarching administrative framework, with subordinate departments and counties numbering “a hundred and □ a hundred and fifteen” [?]. The passage concerning “□ Shun” is unclear [?]; those who discourse on the Way and virtue number “not more than ten thousand” [?]. Added to them are the outstanding men among the clerks and common people, and disciples [the intervening wording is corrupt or illegible]. They raise their spirits and hope to achieve something [?] in an age when the Way prevails, lifting their heads [?] to present themselves for examination. The educational authorities selected only sixteen hundred and some additional candidates. When these were examined, barely one in ten succeeded. The five examination rooms each assessed one Classic. The chief examiners scrutinized the work, opening and reading it again and again, examining everything carefully. [An illegible character] the wording was rigorous and the meaning correct, checked against the Classics of the sages and worthies…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
七髮無戾方在甄錄矣
盟鬼神慎核其尤止
人遵
從學所選又未及十
焉此外雖有詞嚴誼
不背經傳者亦忍而棄
□是褫其難矣
===
示程其文章獻
傳播四方垂示不朽
□而賓興之鄉里親
供帳迎歸邸第有司
事以表其閭同袍之
有先著鞭之羡鄉里
punctuated:
七髮無戾，方在甄錄矣。盟鬼神，慎核其尤，止人遵從學所選，又未及十焉。此外雖有詞嚴誼不背經傳者，亦忍而棄。□是褫其難矣。
示程其文章獻，傳播四方，垂示不朽。□而賓興之，鄉里親供帳，迎歸邸第。有司事以表其閭，同袍之有先著鞭之羡，鄉里
translation_en:
…Only then were they considered for selection, being without deviation [?; the opening characters 七髮 are unclear]. Pledging before the spirits, we carefully scrutinized the outstanding candidates. Those selected through learning [?; 止人遵從學所選 is garbled] numbered fewer than ten. Beyond these, even those whose language was dignified and whose meaning did not depart from the classics and their commentaries were reluctantly discarded. □ This … its difficulty [?; 褫其難 is unclear].
Their writings were displayed as models and presented [?], circulated throughout the realm, and handed down as enduring examples. □ They were then honored as guests and recommended for advancement. Their relatives and fellow villagers prepared a welcoming reception and escorted them back to their residences. The responsible officials took steps to honor their neighborhood gates [?]. Their fellows envied them for having taken the lead, and their fellow villagers …

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
□推本其父祖厥德之
榮矣哉多士焚膏繼
垢磨光極力於燈窻
者不計年歲無非工
章求遂於主司而朔
榮也今既遂所願矣
□夫習乎身則
===
□及乎物則爲
用也有文章無政事
體而無用有體無用
有政事無文章則有
無體有用無體則繆
行將上南宮對
□膴仕其榮益非今日
punctuated: □推本其父祖厥德之榮矣哉！多士焚膏繼垢磨光，極力於燈窻者，不計年歲，無非工章求遂於主司而朔榮也。今既遂所願矣，□夫習乎身則□，及乎物則爲用也。有文章無政事，體而無用；有體無用。有政事無文章，則有無體；有用無體則繆。行將上南宮，對□，膴仕，其榮益非今日
translation_en: …□Tracing this back to the virtue of their fathers and ancestors—what an honor! The many scholars burn lamp oil, continue through grime, and polish themselves [?], exerting themselves by lamplit windows for years beyond counting. All seek, through accomplished writing, to gain acceptance from the presiding examiners and attain honor [?]. Now they have fulfilled their wishes. □What is cultivated in oneself is □; when extended to others, it becomes practical application. Literary accomplishment without administrative achievement is substance without application: there is substance but no application. Administrative achievement without literary accomplishment, however, means having [application?] without substance [?]; application without substance is misguided. Soon you will proceed to the Ministry of Rites for the Metropolitan Examination, respond to □, and enter high office. Your honor will then surpass that of today…

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
也毋忘以政文章之心
政事務殫心思竭智
下爲民以皐夔稷契
周召爲丕式務使今
文章徵而爲他日之
政事皆自今
===
舉措之無相
以業不患不著於時
不患不加於民聲名
不昭之簡冊大書高
階重祿
有寵錫之典而榮庸
手展是錄而觀者指
上心
punctuated: 也。毋忘以政文章之心，政事務殫心思、竭智，下爲民，以皐、夔、稷、契、周、召爲丕式。務使今文章徵而爲他日之政事，皆自今舉措之無相，以業不患不著於時，不患不加於民，聲名不昭之簡冊，大書高階重祿，有寵錫之典而榮庸。手展是錄而觀者，指上心……
translation_en: …Do not forget the intention with which you approach literary composition [?]. In governmental affairs, devote all your thought and exhaust your understanding; work for the people below, taking Gao, Kui, Ji, Qi, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao as your great exemplars. Strive to ensure that your literary compositions today find their realization in your governmental affairs in days to come. All begins with your actions from this time onward [the ensuing wording is garbled: ?]. With achievement, you need not fear that it will fail to become manifest in your age, nor that its benefits will fail to reach the people. Your reputation will not shine in the historical records [?]; great inscriptions, high rank, and generous emoluments [?], together with ceremonies bestowing imperial favor, will honor your service. Those who unfold this record in their hands and read it will point … [the closing words 指上心 are unclear: ?].

title: 正德二年河南鄉試錄
text:
述行或一言推本於主
等亦與有榮焉若以
爲弁髦一遇富貴利
□學而棄之庸瑣委
榮是謀大非主司以
□之意也大負主司
□神之誠也大
===
揄揚以圖報
主也
附涿州儒學學正秦
□丁
punctuated:
述行，或一言推本於主，等亦與有榮焉。若以爲弁髦，一遇富貴利，□學而棄之，庸瑣委榮是謀，大非主司以□之意也，大負主司□神之誠也。大揄揚以圖報主也。

附：涿州儒學學正秦□丁。
translation_en:
… recounting deeds, or in a single remark tracing their source to the sovereign [?], we too share in the honor. If, however, one regards learning as something disposable, like a discarded ceremonial cap and forelock, and, upon encountering wealth, rank, and profit, abandons it [the wording surrounding □學 is uncertain], pursuing petty concerns and honor [?], this greatly contravenes the chief examiner’s intention in □ and greatly betrays the sincerity with which the chief examiner □ his spirit [?]. Lavishly proclaiming praise, one seeks thereby to repay the sovereign [?].

Appended: Qin □ding, School Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhuozhou.
